title: Emit the genesis value as the back-pointer of a key's first transaction

rule.text: A signer with no prior transaction uses the genesis value, SHA-256(the signer's keyhash) — over the 32 keyhash bytes themselves, not over a CBOR encoding of them — derivable by any verifier

given: A key K generated for the test with no transaction in its archive, and a counterparty P with an existing chain and a proof-of-presence record between K and P.
when: K signs its first transaction through the archive component: an adoption of K under P, K in field 1, field 8 naming that record.
then: The adoption's key 0 list for K is exactly one 32-byte value equal to SHA-256 over the 32 bytes of K's keyhash. A verifier recomputing that value from K's keyhash reports K's chain as rooted at genesis at this record.

title: Advance both signers' chains by an adoption, one back-pointer list per signer in signer order

rule.text: One back-pointer LIST per required signer, since each signer has their own independent archive. An adoption advances both the node's archive and the patron's.
Signer order is the order the type's own schema introduces its required signers

given: Node N whose archive head is h_N and patron P whose archive head is h_P, each the txid of an earlier transaction; a proof-of-presence record between them.
when: N and P sign an adoption of N under P; afterwards N signs a departure from P and P signs a disavowal of another subordinate.
then: The adoption's key 0 is [[h_N], [h_P]] in that order, node then patron. N's departure carries key 0 [[txid(adoption)]] and P's disavowal carries key 0 [[txid(adoption)]]: each signer's next record back-points to the adoption.

title: Report a chain that does not reach back when a signer's back-pointer names another signer's record

rule.text: Getting this wrong is silent. Every hash and signature still verifies while each predecessor is attributed to the wrong signer, so a mismatch surfaces only when someone walks a chain and finds it does not reach back.

given: N (head h_N) and P (head h_P) as in ARC-02, and an adoption of N under P whose key 0 is [[h_P], [h_N]], the two lists swapped, signed by both parties.
when: The adoption is verified structurally, then a walker follows N's chain backward from the adoption, fetching each named predecessor.
then: Structural verification does not report the adoption malformed. The walk of N's chain fetches h_P, finds that N is not a signer of that record, and reports N's chain as not reaching back past the adoption; it reports no complete prefix for N from that head.
interpretation: The section names the symptom, a walked chain that does not reach back, and no verdict word; the test reads a fetched predecessor that the named signer did not sign as that symptom, reported distinctly from malformed.

title: Open a relationship's series at counter 0 on adoption and advance it strictly on departure

rule.text: a new adoption establishes its relationship's series, countersigned by the same party a reissue would need
counter incremented within the current series
Within one series a new counter must be strictly greater than the last one the verifier holds

given: Node N adopted under patron P, the adoption's field 3 locator carrying seqno {s, 0}; an observer O holding that adoption and nothing else in series s.
when: N signs a departure from P and O verifies it.
then: The departure's field 3 is {s, c} with the same series s and c strictly greater than 0; O accepts it as newer than the adoption within series s. A second departure from N carrying {s, c} again, with different contents, is not accepted as newer.

title: Accept a departure whose counter skips values in its series, and one in a series with no prior state

rule.text: not exactly previous+1, since a verifier may legitimately have missed intervening transactions and requiring contiguity would reject valid updates. Absence of prior state is not a failure.

given: Observer O holds N's adoption under P at seqno {s, 0} and nothing else in series s, and holds no record at all in series s2.
when: O verifies a departure of N from P carrying seqno {s, 7}, and separately a departure carrying seqno {s2, 5}.
then: Both are accepted: the gap from 0 to 7 within s is not reported as an error, and the record in s2 is not rejected for O holding no prior state in that series or ranked against the record in s.

title: Accept a record timed at its predecessor's effective time or far ahead of the verifier's clock

rule.text: It is a floor, and not a rate limit. Everything at or after the predecessor's effective time is admissible, including days in the future
Timestamps are not checked against a local clock at structural verification.

given: Node N whose archive head is a transaction with timestamp t0, and a verifier whose local clock reads t_now, with t0 not later than t_now.
when: N signs two departures back-pointing to that head, one with timestamp exactly t0 and one with timestamp t_now plus thirty days; the verifier checks each.
then: Both verify as structurally valid; neither is reported malformed.

title: Carry both branch heads in the next ordinary transaction after the archive forks

rule.text: A signer whose archive has forked — typically from concurrent use of two devices — reunites it by supplying both branch heads in the next ordinary transaction.
Merge automatically on noticing divergence.

given: A client for N holding two heads of its own archive, h_a and h_b, neither reachable from the other: two records each back-pointing to the same earlier record of N.
when: The client signs its next ordinary transaction, a departure.
then: The departure's key 0 list for N contains exactly h_a and h_b, sorted ascending bytewise; a walker from the departure reaches both branches and reports no unsatisfied back-pointer; no separate merge object is emitted.

title: Serve an archive fetch head-first in batches that continue from the previous reply's oldest record

rule.text: Paginate by re-requesting with field 2 set to the previous reply's field 4.
records in reverse chain order, head first

given: Subject S holding an unbroken chain of R records rooted at genesis and serving its own archive; the requester asks for max_records m, 1 to 256, with R greater than m so that more than one batch is needed.
when: A requester sends ArchiveRequest {1: S, 2: S's head, 3: m, 5: nonce}, then re-requests with field 2 set to each reply's field 4 until a reply's field 3 is false.
then: Every reply's field 1 equals its request's nonce. The first reply's first envelope has txid equal to the requested head. Within each reply, each record's back-pointer list for S names the record that follows it. Each non-final reply's field 4 is the txid of its oldest record. The batches concatenated are the whole chain, and only the last reply's field 3 is false.

title: Reject an archive batch whose back-pointers do not match the records that follow

rule.text: The requester verifies the chain itself. Each returned record's back-pointers must match the record that follows it in the batch, and the first must match the requested head.

given: A holder answering for subject S, and a requester asking with field 2 set to S's head.
when: The holder returns a batch in which one middle record has been replaced by another record of S that the preceding record's back-pointer does not name; in a second run the batch's first record is not the requested head.
then: In the first run the requester reports the batch as failing chain verification at the first mismatching record, and the records from that point on are not reported as a verified prefix. In the second run it fails at record one.

title: Treat a short archive reply as no evidence about the archive's length

rule.text: A holder may refuse a request or return fewer records than asked for; a short reply is not evidence of a short archive, and a patron must not treat it as truncation.

given: A requester holding S's head and asking for max_records m; a holder that returns k records, k less than m, whose oldest record's back-pointer names a record not in the batch, once with field 3 true and once with field 3 false.
when: The requester processes each reply.
then: In both runs the requester's result marks the verified range as ending at an unfetched predecessor and does not record S's archive as beginning at the oldest returned record or as rooted at genesis; when the test continues, the requester's next request names the oldest returned record in field 2.

title: Mark an archive restored without a requested head as internally verified but not verified-complete

rule.text: Where field 2 was absent, there is no requested head to match: the chain still verifies internally, but its newestness is the holder's claim and nothing the requester holds can check it
never present a restored archive as verified-complete

given: A client for S that has lost its archive and holds no head; a holder serving S's chain from a record the holder claims as newest.
when: The client sends ArchiveRequest with field 2 absent and fetches the chain to its end.
then: The client reports the chain as internally verified, every back-pointer matching the following record, and its status is distinguishable from a head-verified fetch: the restored archive is not marked verified-complete and the newest record is recorded as the holder's claim.

title: Verify a history presented from an earlier head as an unbroken prefix

rule.text: Any presented sequence is provably unbroken across the range shown, even though the archive is built and held by the subject.
Presenting less history means presenting an earlier head; there is no other way to truncate, and none is needed.

given: Subject S with a chain of R records rooted at genesis whose newest record is r_R; a patron evaluating an adoption of S.
when: S presents adoption field 7 = txid(r_j) for some j less than R, and the patron walks back from it, fetching from S.
then: The walk reports the range r_j back to genesis as unbroken and rooted at genesis. The records after r_j are neither fetched nor reported missing, and the presentation is not rejected for naming a head that is not S's newest record.

title: Stop a backward walk at a series reissue and report it as the presented range's root

rule.text: supplies that root, asserting that history existed across the boundary without carrying what it contained, so the chain before it need not be retained or presented
That range is rooted at identity genesis, or at a checkpoint attesting that history existed before it

given: Subject S whose chain contains a patron-countersigned series reissue r_c, and whose records before r_c S no longer holds; a patron walking back from S's head.
when: The walk reaches r_c and requests its predecessor, which S does not serve.
then: The result names the range from the head to r_c as unbroken and r_c as the range's root, a checkpoint distinguished from genesis; the unfetched record before r_c is reported as lying beyond the checkpoint, and no record is reported malformed.
interpretation: The design says a checkpoint supplies a root and wire-format.md §3.4 says an unfetchable predecessor is incomplete rather than malformed; the test reads a stop at a countersigned reissue as a result distinct from a stop at an ordinary unfetchable record, which no sentence states.

title: Evaluate a presented archive by the counterparties the patron already knows and nothing else

rule.text: Records naming identities you have never heard of are not weak evidence; they are no evidence
Do not compute a total.

given: The reference patron policy on infra node P, whose known identities are the set K; two unbroken presented chains for subject S: chain A whose counterparties are all in K, and chain B equal to A plus many records whose counterparties are all outside K. Weighing an archive is policy per infra-client-requirements.md §5; the test binds the reference policy only.
when: P evaluates each chain at adoption.
then: The initial trust state P derives for S is identical for A and B. The result carries no field for archive length, record count or counterparty count.

title: Report a fork and notify both patrons when currency assertions for one identity diverge

rule.text: A conforming inquirer who receives divergent assertions notifies both patrons.
What a caller can learn is a fork: two patrons attesting competing claims is visible-but-unresolved, and that is the point

given: An inquirer I outside the horizon of identity X, holding two introductions for X whose locators name patrons P1 and P2 respectively; P1 and P2 each answer a currency query for X with an attestation whose field 2, the current key, differs from the other's.
when: I issues the currency query to both and receives both attestations.
then: I's result for X reports a fork: both attestations are retained and neither is silently chosen as X's current key. I sends a notification to P1 and a notification to P2.
interpretation: The notice is unspecified (design §22.3 item 3 records it as open); the test observes that a message is sent to each patron and checks neither its content nor its encoding.

title: Keep presence records, sealed captures and seeds when the chain is pruned at a checkpoint

rule.text: Pruning the chain must not delete presence records, sealed captures or capture seeds.
Pruning is therefore permitted only beyond the window

given: A client for S whose chain holds a patron-countersigned series reissue r_c dated more than 730 days ago, with presence records before r_c, each with a sealed capture and a capture seed in the local store.
when: The user prunes the chain at r_c through the client's deliberate retention control.
then: A backward walk from S's head now stops at r_c and the chain records before it are no longer served. Every presence record, sealed capture and capture seed dated before r_c is still present in the local store and returned by lookup by txid.

title: Advance one chain per key across every binding, partitioned by series

rule.text: One chain per key, spanning every binding.
one series per patron relationship
subject whose archive is wanted

given: Subject S adopted under patron P1 and then under P2, and has signed a presence record in each relationship.
when: A holder fetches S's archive with an ArchiveRequest naming S and no head.
then: One chain is returned whose records back-point across both relationships in signing order; the records under P1 carry one series and those under P2 another, each opened at counter 0 by its adoption.

title: Obtain the strongest proximity channel the hardware supports and record which was achieved

rule.text: Obtain the strongest proximity channel the hardware supports
record which channel it got

given: Two clients on a harness whose device layer offers NFC and optical channels and no UWB.
when: They run a presence ceremony to completion.
then: The finalized record's proximity channels carry an NFC entry as the strongest achieved, and no UWB entry.

title: Never present a weaker channel as a stronger one

rule.text: Never present a weaker channel as a stronger one
No implementation should treat any single channel as proof that a counterparty's key is physically present.

given: Two clients on a harness whose device layer offers only the optical channel.
when: They run a presence ceremony to completion.
then: The record's proximity channels carry optical and nothing ranked above it; no NFC or UWB entry appears.

title: Run the guided capture with randomised prompts, three to five images over ten to fifteen seconds

rule.text: Randomised prompts, 3-5 images over 10-15 seconds
The gain comes from diversity, not count.

given: A client capturing its counterparty on the harness, run twice with independent randomness. The figures are chosen values (design §21).
when: Each capture sequence runs.
then: Each sealed capture holds between three and five frames whose timestamps span between ten and fifteen seconds, and the two runs' prompt sequences differ.

title: Derive the capture key exactly as specified

rule.text: The derivation is HKDF-SHA-256, exactly
salt empty, IKM the seed, info the ASCII tag `rhtn/1:capture` followed by the raw 32-byte subject and holder keyhashes and the raw 32-byte ceremony pre-commitment, output length 32

given: A fixed seed, subject keyhash, holder keyhash and ceremony pre-commitment.
when: The client derives k_capture.
then: The 32 bytes equal HKDF-SHA-256 computed independently with empty salt, the seed as IKM and the stated info; a different holder or ceremony_id yields a different key.

title: Compute the ceremony pre-commitment contributorily, in ascending keyhash order

rule.text: the pre-commitment is the SHA-256 of the ASCII tag `rhtn/1:ceremony` followed by the two contributions in ascending participant-keyhash order
neither party can force a repeat

given: Two clients each contributing 16 fixed random bytes over the direct channel, with participant keyhashes in known order.
when: Both compute the pre-commitment.
then: Both produce the same 32 bytes, equal to SHA-256 of the tag followed by the contributions ordered by ascending participant keyhash, and changing either contribution changes the value.

title: Hold no decryptable likeness and no sealing key once the capture is sealed

rule.text: Seal captures under the capture key the subject supplied, discard it once the capture is sealed, and never retain a key released later
A compliant client holds no decryptable likeness of another person

given: Client B has completed a ceremony with A and sealed its captures of A. The biometric engine, template format and sealed-store AEAD parameters are undecided (design §22.2) and are supplied to the test as parameters.
when: The test inspects B's persistent storage and asks B to open A's capture without a grant.
then: Storage holds the sealed capture and A's seed for B's own captures only; no plaintext frame, no plaintext template and no k_capture for A's capture is present, and the open attempt fails.

title: Retain no released key after answering

rule.text: never retain a key released later
An absent capture key is `unavailable`, not `inconclusive`

given: Verifier B answered a consented query about A using a KeyGrant A sent.
when: A second consented query about the same record arrives with no new grant, and the test inspects B's storage.
then: The released key is absent from storage and the second query is answered `unavailable`.

title: Open only the capture the grant names and keep the others sealed

rule.text: the grant names the one to open
A ceremony seals a new capture; it does not replace an earlier one.

given: Verifier B holds two sealed captures of A from records R1 and R2, each under its own seed.
when: A consented query arrives with a KeyGrant whose field 1 is R2's txid.
then: B answers from R2's capture; R1's capture is still sealed afterwards and R1's key was never derived.

title: Grant against the most recent eligible capture by default

rule.text: Querying prefers the most recent eligible capture
when you are the subject releasing a key, the most recent eligible capture is the default

given: Subject A has met verifier B twice, in records R1 then R2, both eligible, and has set no preference.
when: A's client releases a capture key for a query directed at B.
then: The KeyGrant's field 1 is R2's txid.

title: Treat a grant unattached to a countersigned query as malformed

rule.text: A grant arriving unattached to a query the subject countersigned is an unsolicited key release; treat one as malformed rather than opening your store.
Field 2 binds the grant to a query.

given: Verifier B holds a sealed capture of A. No query about A has arrived, and the buffering bound is the test's parameter since the wire leaves it local.
when: A KeyGrant from A naming that record and a query_id B has not seen arrives, and the bound elapses.
then: B opens nothing, answers nothing, and the grant is discarded when the bound elapses.

title: Reject a grant from anyone but the subject, and let the first authenticated grant stand

rule.text: The authenticated sender MUST be the subject
Duplicates are ignored, and so is a differing second grant for a query already satisfied

given: Verifier B holds a consented query about A. A grant for it arrives from C, then a valid grant from A, then a differing grant from A for the same query.
when: B processes the three in order.
then: The grant from C is rejected and opens nothing; the first grant from A is used to answer; the third changes nothing and B's answer is not revised.

title: Answer `unavailable` for a grant naming a record you do not hold

rule.text: A grant naming a record the holder does not hold yields `unavailable`

given: Verifier B holds no sealed capture for record R, and a consented query about A names R in its grant.
when: The grant and query arrive.
then: B's signed response carries result `unavailable`.

title: Reject a query without consent, or not addressed to you, by closing the stream

rule.text: a query arriving without consent is rejected
a receiving verifier rejects a query not addressed to it before any processing
No verifier may answer an identity-comparison request unless the subject of that request has signed it.

given: Verifier B receives, on separate type-4 streams, a query with no consent beside it, a query whose consent does not verify under the subject, and a query whose field 7 names another verifier.
when: B processes each.
then: Each stream is closed with no VerifierResponse sent, and no comparison is run for any of them.

title: Deliver a copy of your signed response to the subject

rule.text: A response about a subject is also delivered to that subject
a verifier answering a query about subject S sends a copy of its signed response to S as well as to the querier

given: Verifier B answers a consented query from C about subject A.
when: B sends its response.
then: The signed VerifierResponse reaches C, and a copy with identical bytes reaches A over the association the grant established.

title: Report a failed decryption as `inconclusive`, never as `no-match`

rule.text: `inconclusive` covers a failure to decrypt, and `no-match` never does.
Report a decryption failure as `inconclusive`, never as `no-match`.
Truncated or unauthenticated ciphertext is a decryption failure

given: Verifier B's sealed capture of A has been truncated on disk, and a consented query with a valid grant arrives. The biometric engine, template format and sealed-store AEAD parameters are undecided (design §22.2) and are supplied to the test as parameters.
when: B attempts to open and compare.
then: B's signed response carries `inconclusive` with basis 0 and the query's template version, and never `no-match`.

title: Reject a second, different profile within one ceremony

rule.text: one profile per ceremony, or the verifier rejects
can require that all queries from one ceremony carry the identical profile

given: Verifier B has answered a consented query bound to ceremony pre-commitment P carrying profile F1.
when: A second consented query bound to P arrives carrying a different profile F2.
then: B rejects it and sends no second response for that ceremony.
interpretation: Whether the subject's client also refuses to countersign a differing second profile is stated as a capability rather than a rule, so only the verifier side is asserted.

title: Query verifiers and answer queries without asking the operator

rule.text: Query verifiers automatically.
the witness's client observes a ceremony, tests the evidence and signs without pausing for its operator's approval
A's operator is not asked and is not told

given: A ceremony on the harness with a prompt hook that records every operator interaction on every client, including the verifiers'.
when: The ceremony runs and its queries are answered.
then: Queries are issued and answered, and the hook records no prompt to any operator for querying, witnessing or answering; the verifier's operator receives no notification.
interpretation: design §7.3 (the verifier's operator is not told they were sampled) and design §19.6 (a verifier is told, at the moment they are asked, that answering records them in a third party's evidence) pull in opposite directions for the verifier. The reference client raises §19.6's disclosure as a notice carrying no ceremony, subject or querier, and asks nothing; this test reads 'no notification' as no prompt and no notice naming the ceremony. Which of the two the author intends is open.

title: Withhold disclosable fields by default, and let the digests travel

rule.text: Withhold a presence record's disclosable fields by default
The digest count and labels always travel, so a recipient knows a field exists and was withheld.

given: Client A holds a finalized record with all seven disclosable fields, and has given no instruction to reveal.
when: A presents the record to a party that is not a prospective patron.
then: The presentation reveals none of the seven fields and carries every field's digest and label, and the envelope signature verifies over it.

title: Withhold your envelope signature from a body omitting a response you hold

rule.text: Withhold your envelope signature from a proposed body omitting a verifier response you hold
a subject holding a response withholds its envelope signature from a proposed body that omits it

given: Subject A holds a copy of verifier B's response about A, delivered by B; the counterparty proposes a final body without it.
when: A's client is asked to sign the proposed body.
then: No envelope signature by A is produced for that body; a body that includes B's response is signed.

title: Refuse to sign a record attributing to you a witness you did not nominate

rule.text: Refuse to sign a record attributing to you a witness you did not nominate

given: Participant A nominated witnesses W1 and W2; the proposed body attributes W3 to A.
when: A's client is asked to sign.
then: No envelope signature by A is produced; the same body with W3 attributed to the counterparty is signed.

title: Tell the user when your own nominees are absent or outnumbered

rule.text: Check the `nominated_by` split before you sign, and tell the user when your own nominees are absent or outnumbered.

given: Participant A nominated two witnesses; the proposed body carries five witnesses of which one is A's, with a notification hook on A's client.
when: A's client checks the split before signing.
then: The hook records a notice to the user that A's nominees are outnumbered, before any signature is produced.
interpretation: The form of the notice is not specified; the test asserts that one is raised before signing.

title: Decline to witness a ceremony whose claimed start is far from your clock

rule.text: Decline to witness a ceremony whose claimed `started_at` is far from the time you observe.

given: Witness W with tolerance T, chosen by the test since the requirement leaves it to the witness, is nominated for a ceremony whose started_at is more than T from W's clock.
when: W's client is asked to sign.
then: No witness signature by W is produced; the same ceremony with started_at within T is signed.

title: Strip metadata from captured images before sealing

rule.text: Strip metadata from captured images before storing them, and do not rely on camera-pipeline defaults.

given: The harness camera returns frames carrying EXIF location, timestamp and device identifiers. The biometric engine, template format and sealed-store AEAD parameters are undecided (design §22.2) and are supplied to the test as parameters.
when: Client B captures and seals, and the test opens the capture with the subject's key.
then: No frame in the opened capture carries EXIF or other metadata.

title: Send the capture key directly to the selected verifier

rule.text: Send the capture key directly to a selected verifier
bypassing the counterparty running the ceremony and every witness

given: Subject A in a ceremony run by C, with witnesses observing; C selects B as a verifier for A.
when: A's client releases the capture key.
then: The KeyGrant is observed only on A's end-to-end path to B; no grant bytes appear on any path to C or to a witness.

title: Keep the anti-oracle aggregate as a lock, not a log

rule.text: A counter per requester and per ceremony window, discarded when the window closes
The aggregate is a lock, not a log.

given: Subject A, with the ceremony window W chosen by the test.
when: During W a requester exceeds the per-requester limit; after W closes the test inspects A's storage.
then: The excess query receives no grant, and after W no record of the requester or of the count remains.

title: Disclose at capture time what the record will contain and who can read it

rule.text: Tell participants what the record will contain and who will be able to read it

The reference client must disclose to a verifier or witness, at the moment they are asked, that their identity and relationship will be permanently recorded in a third party's evidence and readable by future evaluators.

given: A ceremony on the harness with a notification hook on the participants', witnesses' and verifiers' clients.
when: The ceremony reaches capture and the witnesses and verifiers are asked.
then: The hook records a disclosure to each participant before capture, and to each witness and verifier at the moment it is asked.
interpretation: The content and form of the disclosure are not specified; the test asserts its occurrence and timing.

title: Count qualifying bundle records once by txid when computing n

rule.text: count qualifying ones once by txid
Compute n over the bundle handed to you, and treat it as your counterparty's claim

given: A bundle handed to the selector containing four qualifying records, two of them the same record twice.
when: The selector computes n.
then: n is 3, and the required response count follows from 3.

title: Answer `unavailable` to a claimed `met` your own records refute

rule.text: A claimed `met` the verifier's own records refute is answered `unavailable`

given: Verifier B holds no record of ever having met selector C, and a consented query from C arrives with selection basis 0.
when: B processes the query.
then: B's signed response carries `unavailable` and no comparison is run.

title: Keep a late response beside its record, never inside it, and discard it with the record

rule.text: It does not amend the record it names.
The response must carry a `query_id` the subject countersigned for that ceremony
Retention follows the record it supplements.

given: A holder keeps record R; a LateResponse naming R with a countersigned query_id arrives, then one with an unconsented query_id.
when: The holder processes both, then later discards R.
then: R's bytes and txid are unchanged; the first LateResponse is held beside R and the second is rejected; after R is discarded the LateResponse is gone too.

title: Issue a fresh patron attestation for a subordinate, signed under the currency tag

rule.text: Issue currency attestations for subordinates
~10 h default; hours, not days

given: Infra node P has adopted S, whose current key is k. The attestation lifetime L is chosen by the test, since design §21.1 leaves its value unset.
when: S requests currency from P.
then: A CurrencyReply with code 0 carries an attestation whose field 1 is S, field 2 is k, field 5 is 0, field 6 is P, whose field 4 minus field 3 equals L, and whose COSE_Sign1 verifies under P's classical key with external_aad rhtn/1:currency.

title: Refresh by issuing anew, never by extending

rule.text: Issue fresh, never extend stale.
There is no "extend" operation and no field for one, deliberately.

given: S holds an attestation A from P, issued at t0.
when: S requests currency from P again at t1 > t0.
then: The reply's attestation has field 3 later than A's field 3 and a signature different from A's. No message from P carries A's fields 1 to 3 with a later field 4.

title: Issue nothing for a key you have superseded

rule.text: Issue only for the key you currently record.
after it you have nothing to issue for the old key and MUST NOT

given: P recorded S under k1, then received and verified a recovery adoption binding S to k2.
when: A CurrencyRequest naming S arrives at P.
then: Every attestation P issues for S afterwards carries k2 in field 2; none carries k1.

title: Answer a request you cannot issue for with code 1, not with an invented attestation and not with silence

rule.text: So the answers are: an attestation, or nothing.
Code 1 says the responder cannot issue rather than inventing one

given: Node P holds no record of subject X.
when: A CurrencyRequest naming X with nonce n arrives on an authenticated session.
then: A CurrencyReply is observed with field 1 equal to n, field 2 equal to 1 and field 3 absent.

title: Withdrawn: fail closed on a trust-bearing operation while the counterparty's staple is expired or missing
given: Withdrawn.
when: Withdrawn.
then: Withdrawn.
interpretation: Withdrawn 2026-09-10. No staple gates any operation (design §12.6.5, author ruling of that date): stapling supports routing only, and the adoption this entry withheld proceeds. Replaced by CUR-14.

title: Fail open for routine payload when the staple is expired

rule.text: Nothing waits on a staple
A light client offline for a day arrives with a stale staple, receives its messages and transacts

given: Client S attaches to its serving node holding only an expired staple.
when: Queued payload for S is available for delivery.
then: Delivery proceeds. An implementation that withholds routine payload until currency is refreshed fails.

title: Serve nothing under a binding you hold supersession evidence for, whatever the staple says

rule.text: Fail-open is for ignorance, never for knowledge
MUST NOT continue serving it

1 sibling (secondhand)

2 grandpatron

when: S requests currency from G.

given: Withdrawn.
when: Withdrawn.
then: Withdrawn.

rule.text: Nothing is retained on either side.
It is not archived
answered and discarded, and never archived (§10)

given: Node P answers a CurrencyRequest naming S from an authenticated peer Q.

then: No record of the request, of Q, or of the reply is present.

rule.text: Expiry is decided against the relying party's own clock

given: Node N holds an attestation for X with field 4 equal to T. The issuer's clock plays no part in the test.
when: N evaluates the staple with its clock set before T, then with its clock set after T.

rule.text: no trust transaction or user operation is gated on it
Unilateral departure plus adoption elsewhere is the escape hatch

requiring nobody's authority

title: Feed the ladder from the detector, and open its rungs by outage duration

rule.text: Sibling issuance from replicated state, marked secondhand and weighted slightly lower
Grandpatron issuance. It holds the adoption record anyway
Nothing; staple still valid

given: Grandpatron G holds sessions with patron P and P's sibling P', whose heartbeats stop; S, P's subordinate, holds a session upstream to P, whose heartbeats toward S stop too. The intervals before each rung opens are the node's own numbers.

interpretation: The design keys the table on outage duration in words, hours to days and days; the intervals are taken as the operator's numbers, the reference node using the attestation lifetime and two days.

title: Return malformed for every proper prefix of a valid object without crashing

rule.text: CBOR (RFC 8949) with deterministic encoding, RFC 8949 §4.2.
Definite-length encoding only. No indefinite-length arrays, maps or strings.
Bounds exist to stop a stranger exhausting memory, not to describe normal operation.

given: The accept set: every corpus.json entry of class `bytes` whose expect.outcome is `accept` (162 byte-class entries in the current corpus, the accept subset among them). For each entry, every proper prefix of its bytes, lengths 0 to n−1, and memory budget M and per-input time budget T, which no document sets (design §21.1 places buffer bounds with the component and lists none).
when: Each prefix is presented to the decoder as a complete input, at whichever layer the entry's expect.kind names (body, envelope, frame, reply, record).
then: Every prefix yields structural = malformed. The decoder returns a verdict for every prefix; the process neither terminates abnormally nor hangs beyond T nor exceeds M on any of them.
interpretation: An incomplete CBOR data item is not well-formed under RFC 8949; the profile adopts RFC 8949 without restating well-formedness, so the malformed verdict on a truncated item rests on the RFC rather than on a sentence of the profile.

title: Return a verdict for every seeded mutation of a valid object without crashing

rule.text: Bounds exist to stop a stranger exhausting memory, not to describe normal operation.
They are conservative ceilings chosen to bound a decoder's exposure to a hostile peer, set well above any use anyone has articulated.
Validate the bytes as received; do not decode and re-encode to compare.

given: The accept set as in DEC-01. For each entry, N variants produced by a seeded mutator — single-byte substitution, byte insertion, byte deletion, and splicing a run of another entry's bytes into it — with the seed S and N recorded so the run is reproducible; memory budget M and per-input time budget T, which no document sets (design §21.1 places buffer bounds with the component and lists none).
when: Each variant is presented to the decoder as a complete input at the entry's layer.
then: Every variant yields exactly one of structural = valid or structural = malformed. No variant terminates the process abnormally, runs beyond T, or drives memory above M. Any variant reported valid is re-checked by re-serialisation: its emitted bytes equal the variant's bytes.
interpretation: Crash-freedom and a time bound are not stated in any document; §1.3 states only that the bounds exist to stop memory exhaustion by a hostile peer. The test parameterises M and T and records them with the run.

title: Reject a header that declares more content than the input carries, within the memory budget

rule.text: Bounds exist to stop a stranger exhausting memory, not to describe normal operation.
Arrays arriving from strangers are a resource attack surface, so each is given an explicit maximum below; exceeding it is malformed, not merely unusual.
Definite-length encoding only. No indefinite-length arrays, maps or strings.

given: Three inputs derived from the accepted adoption P-adopt-min: (a) the keyhash in field 1 replaced by a byte-string header `5b ffffffffffffffff` (2^64−1 declared bytes) followed by 32 bytes; (b) the merge back-pointer list in field 0 replaced by an array header `9a ffffffff` (2^32−1 declared elements) followed by one element; (c) the body's map header replaced by `ba ffffffff` followed by the original entries. memory budget M and per-input time budget T, which no document sets (design §21.1 places buffer bounds with the component and lists none).
when: Each input is presented to the decoder as a complete body.
then: structural = malformed for all three. Peak memory during each decode stays within M, which is set far below the declared sizes; the decoder returns rather than waiting for the declared content.
interpretation: The specification bounds memory through the array ceilings and says bounds exist to stop exhaustion; that a declared length beyond the input or beyond any ceiling is rejected on sight, without reserving the declared size, is implied by that purpose rather than stated.

title: Reject a self-describe CBOR tag prefixed to a message

rule.text: Nested COSE objects are UNTAGGED. RFC 9052 permits either, and libraries expose both serialisations, so a profile that does not choose gets two byte encodings for one object
Validate the bytes as received; do not decode and re-encode to compare.
Signature coverage is the body map only. Never the envelope, or signatures would not survive the addition of a signer.

given: The accepted adoption envelope P-adopt-min with the bytes `d9 d9 f7` (CBOR tag 55799, self-describe) prefixed to the envelope; separately, the same envelope's body with the same prefix; separately, the accepted Attach frame P-frame-01 with the prefix inserted after the u32 length prefix (length adjusted).
when: Each tagged form is presented to the decoder at its layer.
then: structural = malformed for all three; none is accepted as the untagged object it wraps. The untagged originals remain accepted.
interpretation: No document names tag 55799. The expectation rests on the schema's top-level item being a map (§3's Envelope, §8.0's frame array) and a tag being a different major type, so a library that strips the tag silently would give one object two accepted encodings — the outcome §1 forbids for nested COSE tags.

title: Accept a presence record at the derived envelope ceiling of 36 signature entries

rule.text: The envelope bound MUST be derived, never asserted independently, and derived in two steps.

Sum the transaction type's per-role bounds to get the logical signer ceiling, then double it for the COSE_Signature array, since each logical signer contributes one classical and one post-quantum entry (§3.5).
For a presence record: 2 participants + 16 witnesses = 18.
Twice the logical-signer bound, since each contributes one classical and one PQ entry (§3.5). For a presence record, 36
Each logical signer contributes exactly two COSE_Signature entries: one under its classical component (alg = -8) and one under its post-quantum component (alg = -49).

given: Eighteen synthetic identities generated by the test-vectors keygen recipe (test-vectors/README.md; the shipped corpus holds fewer than 18, which is why B-witnesses-17 has no 16-witness accept companion at the envelope layer). A normal presence record whose body names 2 participants and 16 witnesses, with a full envelope of 18 logical signers — 36 COSE_Signature entries, sorted by kid then classical before post-quantum — every signature real over the body under `rhtn/1:envelope`.
when: The envelope is presented to the decoder and verifier.
then: structural = valid and signatures[signer, alg] = verified for all 36 entries. An implementation carrying an independently asserted envelope ceiling below 36 entries or below 18 logical signers reports malformed here and fails conformance.

title: Accept an array or value exactly at a §1.3 ceiling that no corpus fixture reaches

rule.text: Arrays arriving from strangers are a resource attack surface, so each is given an explicit maximum below; exceeding it is malformed, not merely unusual.
Capabilities value, bytes | 1024
Verifier responses per presence record | 32 — two subjects × a per-subject threshold capped at 10, with headroom.
Verifier responses per recovery | 32

given: Three at-ceiling objects for rows whose corpus coverage is a rejection only: (a) a Capabilities map carrying one value of exactly 1024 encoded bytes (B-caps-value-1025 is the rejection; no 1024 accept exists); (b) a normal presence record carrying 32 verifier responses from 32 distinct synthetic verifiers, 16 per subject, sorted as §4.5 requires (U-responses-33 is the unit-recipe rejection); (c) a recovery adoption carrying 32 verifier responses (U-recovery-responses-33 is the rejection). Identities from the keygen recipe.
when: Each object is presented to the decoder at its layer.
then: structural = valid for all three. An implementation whose ceiling is off by one on the low side — 1023 bytes, or 31 responses — rejects one of these and fails conformance.

title: Reject a CatalogReply carrying 112 entries

rule.text: CatalogReply entries | 111 — an answering node answers for itself plus the ≤110 users it serves
Arrays arriving from strangers are a resource attack surface, so each is given an explicit maximum below; exceeding it is malformed, not merely unusual.

given: The conforming truncated reply P-catalog-reply-truncated, which carries exactly 111 entries in field 2 and a continuation in field 3. A variant appends the withheld 112th entry to field 2, once with field 3 retained and once with field 3 removed. The reply is an unsigned message.
when: Each variant is presented to the decoder as a CatalogReply.
then: structural = malformed for both variants. The 111-entry original remains accepted.

title: Reject an unknown map key on every unsigned message family

rule.text: Unsigned messages reject unknown map keys — every message outside a signature's coverage, in every family.

Unsigned session messages reject unknown map keys (§1's global rule) — CatalogQuery, CatalogReply, ResourceRequest, ResourceResponse and the control frames of §8.0 alike, and equally every unsigned family this chapter does not name: resolution, prekey and archive requests, grants and wrappers.

given: For every unsigned family that has an accepted vector in test-vectors/messages.md — control frames on stream 0, requests, and replies, including CatalogQuery, CatalogReply, ResourceRequest, ResourceResponse, the resolution, prekey and archive messages, grants and wrappers — the vector's top-level map with one added entry `99: h'c0ffee'`, inserted in ascending key position so the map stays canonical; where the message is a frame, the u32 length prefix adjusted.
when: Each modified message is presented to the decoder at its layer.
then: Each is rejected as malformed; none is accepted with the key preserved, and none is accepted with the key ignored. The unmodified vectors remain accepted.

title: Reject an unknown key in the transaction envelope map

rule.text: Unsigned messages reject unknown map keys — every message outside a signature's coverage, in every family.
Signature coverage is the body map only. Never the envelope, or signatures would not survive the addition of a signer.

given: The accepted adoption envelope P-adopt-min with one entry `5: h'c0ffee'` appended to the Envelope map after key 4 (map header `a4` becomes `a5`); the body in field 3 and all four signatures unchanged.
when: The envelope is presented to the decoder and verifier.
then: structural = malformed, even though all four body signatures verify over the unchanged body; the object is not accepted with the envelope-level key preserved.
interpretation: The Envelope map's own keys (version, type, signatures) sit outside every signature's coverage, so §1.2's rule for keys outside a signature's coverage is read as reaching the envelope map; §3 does not say so in as many words, and D2's preservation rule is read as scoped to the signed body.

title: Reject a duplicated unknown extension key

rule.text: No duplicate map keys; a decoder MUST reject them rather than take the last.
Duplicate map keys MUST be rejected before the map is materialised.

given: The accepted extended adoption body P-adopt-extensions (unknown key 99 at the top level and inside the Locator) with the top-level entry `99: h'c0ffee'` repeated once immediately after itself (body map header `a7` becomes `a8`), in two variants: the second value identical, and the second value `h'c0ffef'`.
when: Each variant body is presented to the decoder.
then: structural = malformed for both variants. The single-key original remains accepted. An implementation that collects unknown keys into a list rather than a keyed structure, and so never sees the collision, accepts these and fails.

title: Reject an unknown extension value that is not deterministically encoded

rule.text: Any deterministically encoded CBOR item is admissible — the profile's encoding rules govern the slice's framing, and its meaning is nobody else's to evaluate
Definite-length encoding only. No indefinite-length arrays, maps or strings.
Shortest-form integers.

given: P-adopt-extensions with its top-level key-99 value replaced by, in turn: (a) the indefinite-length array `9f 05 ff`; (b) the non-shortest integer `18 0a`; (c) a byte string with a non-shortest length header `58 03 c0ffee`. Each slice is within the 1024-byte ceiling and the map stays otherwise canonical.
when: Each variant body is presented to the decoder.
then: structural = malformed for all three. An implementation that skips an unknown value by walking its framing without checking the profile's encoding rules inside the slice accepts these and fails.
interpretation: 'The profile's encoding rules govern the slice's framing' is read as requiring the whole slice, not only its outermost header, to be deterministically encoded; whether the protocol-map key rules (unsigned-integer keys, ascending) also reach a map nested inside the slice is a question for the author and is not tested here.

title: Accept a 1024-byte extension value nested 1024 levels deep

rule.text: Any deterministically encoded CBOR item is admissible — the profile's encoding rules govern the slice's framing, and its meaning is nobody else's to evaluate
1024 bytes of encoded CBOR — the complete encoded slice for the value, which is measurable for every value type and is what bounds parser work.

given: P-adopt-extensions with its top-level key-99 value replaced by 1023 bytes of `81` followed by `80` — a deterministic encoding of one-element arrays nested 1024 deep, occupying exactly the 1024-byte extension-value ceiling. memory budget M and per-input time budget T, which no document sets (design §21.1 places buffer bounds with the component and lists none).
when: The body is presented to the decoder.
then: structural = valid; the decoder returns within T and within M; the unknown key's slice is preserved, so the body re-serialises to bytes identical to the input. An implementation with a recursion limit below 1024 reports malformed or terminates abnormally here and fails.
interpretation: §1.3 sets no nesting-depth ceiling; depth is bounded only through the 1024-byte encoded-slice bound, so a decoder that caps depth lower is over-strict under the text as written. Whether the author wants a depth ceiling is raised in the notes.

title: Accept sixteen unknown keys in each of two maps of one body

rule.text: Unknown extension keys per map | 16
Unknown map keys MUST be preserved when re-serializing for signature verification, and MUST NOT be silently dropped.

given: P-adopt-extensions' pattern extended: 16 unknown keys (99 through 114, each `h'c0ffee'`) at the body's top level and 16 unknown keys (the same numbers) inside the Locator map in field 3 — 32 unknown keys in one body, 16 per map, both maps canonical (B-ext-keys-16 exercises one map only).
when: The body is presented to the decoder.
then: structural = valid, and the body re-serialises to bytes identical to the input with all 32 keys present. An implementation counting unknown keys per object rather than per map reports malformed here and fails.
interpretation: 'Per map' is read as each map counted independently, so 32 unknown keys across two maps are within bound; the specification does not say whether the count is per map or per object in any other words.

title: Accept an Attach whose required Capabilities map is empty

rule.text: A required map with no entries is encoded as an empty map — `Capabilities` in `Attach` and `AttachAck` is the case in point, since a peer advertising nothing must still send the field.
This does not apply to required fields.

given: The accepted Attach frame P-frame-01 (two capability parameters, one greased) with field 3 replaced by the empty map `a0`, fields 1 and 2 unchanged, and the u32 length prefix adjusted.
when: The frame is presented to the decoder as a stream-0 control frame.
then: The frame is accepted: structural = valid with an empty capability set. An implementation that applies the omit-if-empty rule to a required field, or requires at least one capability parameter, rejects this and fails.

title: Reject an Attach that omits its required Capabilities map

rule.text: This does not apply to required fields.
A required map with no entries is encoded as an empty map — `Capabilities` in `Attach` and `AttachAck` is the case in point, since a peer advertising nothing must still send the field.

given: P-frame-01 with field 3 removed entirely (Attach map header `a3` becomes `a2`), fields 1 and 2 unchanged, length prefix adjusted. N-shape-attach-missing-identity covers field 1; no fixture covers field 3.
when: The frame is presented to the decoder as a stream-0 control frame.
then: structural = malformed. An implementation that reads the omit-if-empty rule as licensing omission of a required map accepts this and fails.

title: Re-serialise every accepted object to bytes identical to the input

rule.text: Unknown map keys MUST be preserved when re-serializing for signature verification, and MUST NOT be silently dropped.
Keep the received bytes and derive typed views from them.
A signature covers every retained field of the object it signs, except the signature field itself, including unknown extension keys.

given: The accept set: every corpus.json entry of class `bytes` whose expect.outcome is `accept` (162 byte-class entries in the current corpus, the accept subset among them), including P-adopt-extensions (unknown keys top-level and nested), the extended EndpointRecord of records.md (D8) and the SignedLocator carrying unknown key 4 (D9).
when: Each entry is decoded and then emitted again by the implementation's encoder — the same path it uses to reconstruct a signed payload, to store an object, or to hand it onward.
then: For every entry the emitted bytes equal the input bytes exactly, unknown keys, their positions and their encoded values included. No entry is emitted with an unknown key dropped, reordered, or re-encoded.
interpretation: §1.2 states preservation for re-serialisation for signature verification; this entry asserts the same for every re-serialisation the implementation performs, on the reading that a key dropped on any other path yields a different object, and a different txid, at the next holder.

title: Reject entries out of canonical order and any header entry beyond alg and kid

rule.text: entries sort by kid, then classical before post-quantum
A nonempty unprotected header is malformed
Embedded COSE_Sign1 objects omit it

given: A valid adoption envelope; the same with two entries swapped, with one entry's unprotected header nonempty, and with a third protected header entry; and a verifier response whose embedded signatures carry a kid.
when: Each is decoded.
then: The valid envelope is accepted; each variant is rejected at the structural layer before any signature is checked, and the response with a kid in an embedded or standalone signature is rejected. An implementation that tolerates a matching kid there fails.

title: Count the extension bounds in every nested signed map

rule.text: Unknown extension keys per map
the complete encoded slice for the value, which is measurable for every value type and is what bounds parser work

given: A presence record whose first participant map carries sixteen unknown keys, then seventeen; an endpoint record whose first network point carries an unknown value of 1024 encoded bytes, then 1025.
when: Each is decoded.
then: Sixteen keys and 1024 bytes are accepted; seventeen keys and 1025 bytes are rejected, the nested map counted on its own. An implementation counting only the outermost map fails.

title: Rank candidates by available flow, then path length, then consideration order

rule.text: ranks candidates explicitly, by available flow first, then path length, then consideration order
Available flow ranks first

given: A fixed reference graph in which a saturated cut cannot admit every candidate: A carries more flow than B and C; B and C carry equal flow but B is fewer hops from the observer; D and E are equal on both and D was considered first.
when: The reference metric allocates.
then: The allocation admits A before B, B before C, and D before E, and the reported per-candidate flow values match the fixture's expected values.

title: Let no adjacency order decide an equal-path tie

rule.text: at equal path length the winner is then decided by the order edges happen to occupy in the implementation's own adjacency structure
Consideration order breaks true ties only

given: The graph of MET-01 built twice, with its edges inserted in two different orders, and the same consideration order supplied to both.
when: The reference metric allocates over each.
then: Both allocations are identical.

title: Weigh only the intersection with identities you already know

rule.text: A patron following it weighs the intersection and nothing else
records naming unknown identities are not weighed less, they are not weighed

given: The reference policy at patron P, and a presented archive naming three identities P knows and one thousand it does not.
when: P evaluates the archive.
then: The standing P computes equals the standing computed from the three records naming known identities alone, and appending further records naming only unknown identities leaves it unchanged.

title: Substitute a policy without changing anything the protocol does

rule.text: Each node computes its own trust for every known node from the transactions it observes, using the reference algorithm or a variant tuned to its application or group norms.
No pass is promoted to a protocol rule

given: The reference metric and a trivial alternative policy that scores every known node equally, both supplied through the implementation's policy interface.
when: The same observed transactions are fed to a node running each in turn.
then: The two nodes store and forward the same objects and produce the same wire traffic; only their computed standings differ.
interpretation: What the policy interface must expose is not stated; the test asserts that a substitute policy changes computed standing and nothing on the wire.

title: Report a policy's resistance bound from the conformance test

rule.text: provide a conformance test that reports a policy's resistance bound so anyone tuning their own can see what they have given up
Flow-limited trust bounds what any single-entry region can claim regardless of its size (§16.2)

given: The conformance test's fake-region topology, entered beyond the observer's horizon, grown across the population sizes the simulation uses, and two policies: the reference metric and a distance-decay policy.
when: The conformance test runs each policy.
then: For the reference metric the report states a bound equal to the region's cut and the best score never exceeds it at any size. For the decay policy the report states that the score grows with region size.
interpretation: The form of the reported bound is not specified; the test asserts a finite cut-equal bound for the reference and growth for the decay policy.

title: Collapse parallel edges between one pair to one capacity

rule.text: capacity belongs to the pair, not to the count of relationships between them

given: A pair joined by an adoption and two later presence records.
when: The reference metric builds its graph.
then: The pair carries one edge's capacity; summing the three would give a larger flow, and the computed flow equals the single-edge value.

title: Bound the aggregate a set can draw by the cut, per computation

rule.text: the aggregate a set can draw is bounded by the cut (§16.2)
where the entry lies beyond the observer's horizon

given: The simulation's conserving topology: a region behind one acquired peering edge beyond the observer's horizon, at the population sizes the simulation uses.
when: The reference metric computes joint flow to the region and the sum of independent per-target flows.
then: The joint flow saturates at the cut at every size while the independent sum grows with population; the figures match the simulation's committed results.

title: Treat the branching condition as necessary and not sufficient

rule.text: it bounds the hierarchy's fanout and not §16.2.1's unbounded acquaintance degree, so it is necessary and not sufficient

given: Two graphs at the same fanout and the same decay parameter satisfying the condition: one whose acquaintance degree is bounded and one whose acquaintance degree grows with depth.
when: A distance-decay policy is scored on each.
then: The first converges and the second does not, and the conformance report says which; an implementation that reports the condition as sufficient fails.

title: Publish a signed prekey bundle and keep the one-time pool stocked

rule.text: Publish a prekey bundle and keep it stocked.
The bundle is opaque to this protocol

given: Client S attaches to serving node N. The identity binding, prekey cadence and last-resort policy are open integration decisions (design §22.2) and are supplied to the test as parameters.
when: S completes its attach.
then: N holds a PrekeyBundle for S with field 2 equal to 1 and a signature by S under the prekey tag over fields 1 to 4, and a non-empty one-time pool for S.

title: Never serve or use a one-time prekey twice

rule.text: never reuse a one-time prekey
Consume one-time keys on serving them, and only when one is requested.
Only the one-time key is consumed on serving.

given: N holds a pool of one-time keys for S.
when: Two requesters each send a PrekeyRequest for S with field 2 equal to 1.
then: The two replies carry different one-time keys, the pool shrinks by two, and neither key is ever served again.

title: Replenish the one-time pool before it is exhausted

rule.text: Replenish well before exhaustion
Rotate the signed prekey on a policy interval

given: Client S with a replenishment threshold and a signed-prekey interval chosen by the test, since both are policy.
when: Requesters draw one-time keys until the pool falls below the threshold, and the interval elapses.
then: S uploads further one-time keys before the pool reaches zero, and publishes a new bundle with a later field 4 after the interval.

title: Serve reusable material freely and consume nothing unless a one-time key is requested

rule.text: Serve reusable material freely.
The reusable material may be returned any number of times to anyone.

given: N holds S's bundle and pool.
when: Two PrekeyRequests for S with field 2 equal to 0 arrive from different peers.
then: Both replies carry S's bundle, neither carries field 3, and the pool is unchanged.

title: Rate-limit one-time key issuance per requester per subject

rule.text: Rate-limit one-time key issuance per requester per subject.
rate-limits one-time key issuance per requester per subject

given: N with a limit L per requester per subject per window, chosen by the test.
when: One requester sends L plus one PrekeyRequests for S with field 2 equal to 1 within the window, and one for another subject T.
then: The first L replies carry one-time keys; the excess request for S is served no one-time key; the request for T is served one.
interpretation: Whether the refused request is answered with the bundle and no field 3, or with failure code 1, is not stated; the test asserts only that no one-time key is served.

title: Tell the subject when its one-time pool is exhausted

rule.text: Tell the subject when their one-time pool is exhausted.

given: S's pool at N is drained by requesters.
when: The last one-time key is served.
then: S's client learns of the exhaustion and replenishes; the test observes the notice through S's client and the subsequent upload.
interpretation: No wire object carries the exhaustion notice; the test observes it through the client and treats the carrier as a parameter.

title: Prefetch reusable material for the whole Dunbar Org as one sweep

the population swept, in ascending keyhash order
A `PrekeyBatchRequest` naming a population is visibly a sweep

given: Client S attaches with a horizon of known population.
when: S refreshes its prekey material.
then: A PrekeyBatchRequest naming the population in ascending keyhash order is observed, and no single-subject PrekeyRequest with field 2 equal to 0 for any of them.

rule.text: Never prefetch one-time keys.
Request a one-time key only when actually opening a session.

given: Client S has prefetched reusable material for its org and has no session with T.
when: S idles, then sends its first message to T.
then: No PrekeyRequest with field 2 equal to 1 is observed while idle; exactly one, naming T, is observed immediately before the first message.

title: Keep no record of who asked for whose bundle

rule.text: keep no record of who asked for whose bundle

given: N serves several PrekeyRequests and a PrekeyBatchRequest.
when: The test inspects N's persistent storage afterwards.
then: No record of the requesters or of which subjects they asked for is present.

title: Store and serve a bundle without interpreting its contents

rule.text: The bundle is opaque.
The bundle is opaque to this protocol

given: A PrekeyBundle for S whose field 3 is an arbitrary byte string, correctly signed by S.
when: S uploads it and a requester fetches it.
then: N stores and serves it unchanged. An implementation that parses field 3 and rejects it fails.

title: Use the asynchronous construction only leaf to leaf

rule.text: Only leaf-to-leaf needs this.
Leaf → patron | Nothing new.

given: Client S with a session to its patron P and a first message for leaf T.
when: S sends to P and then to T.
then: No prekey request names P and the message to P rides the transport session; a one-time key request names T and the message to T is encrypted under the payload construction.

title: Open a session on reusable material alone when no one-time key remains

rule.text: when none remain, field 3 is simply absent and the session proceeds on reusable material alone

given: T's one-time pool at N is empty.
when: S requests a one-time key for T and then sends its first message.
then: The PrekeyReply carries field 2 and no field 3, and S still opens the session and delivers the message. An implementation that refuses to send without a one-time key fails.

title: Instantiate PQXDH with X25519 and ML-KEM-768 and run the Triple Ratchet, matching the adopted specifications

rule.text: this profile instantiates it with X25519 and ML-KEM-768
Signal's Triple Ratchet.
The requirement below is to adopt it, not to design a replacement.

given: Two clients with fixed key material and the adopted library's published test vectors. The identity binding, prekey cadence and last-resort policy are open integration decisions (design §22.2) and are supplied to the test as parameters.
when: They establish a session and exchange messages.
then: The key agreement and ratchet outputs match the adopted specifications' vectors for the same inputs, and a message decrypts only at its recipient.
interpretation: How the session is bound to the hybrid identity is open; the test parameterises the binding and asserts agreement with the adopted construction's vectors.

title: Dispatch protocol objects and application payload on the end-to-end channel to the right handler

rule.text: Carried as payload, never as a record.
Payload-type demultiplexing.

given: Subject A sends verifier B a KeyGrant and an application message over the same end-to-end session. The demultiplexing scheme is an open decision (design §22.2) supplied as a parameter.
when: B receives both.
then: The KeyGrant reaches B's grant handler and opens the named capture; the application message reaches the application; neither is delivered to the other.
interpretation: The demultiplexing scheme is undecided; the test asserts correct dispatch under whichever scheme is supplied.

title: Deliver payload over the serving node when no direct path exists

rule.text: The relay path is not vestigial and must be maintained as a first-class route.
falls back to the serving node when it fails

given: Two leaves whose NATs, emulated by the harness, defeat hole punching.
when: One sends the other a message.
then: The direct candidates fail and the message is delivered through the serving node's relay; the recipient decrypts it.

title: Let the user override direct versus relayed payload in both directions, with each disclosure stated

rule.text: Direct versus relayed payload must be overridable

given: A release build of the light client.
when: A reviewer opens the payload path setting.
then: Both overrides exist, and the setting states that direct reveals the user's IP to a peer inside the horizon and relayed reveals the communication graph to the serving node.

title: Warn before an authority change that revokes resource access, and list upward-reaching policies on a new patron

rule.text: warn if the resulting topology change will revoke access to resources the user currently uses
When accepting a new patron, list any resources whose policy reaches upward.

given: A release build with the user holding access to resources under the current patron.
when: A reviewer initiates a departure, then accepts a new patron.
then: The departure flow warns and names the resources that will be lost before confirmation; the adoption flow lists resources whose predicates reach upward.

title: Warn that an unlinked identity path abandons standing, and that a linked one loses unlinkability

rule.text: warn that prior standing will be abandoned

given: A release build.
when: A reviewer starts a plain rotation, then a recovery.
then: The plain rotation warns that prior standing is abandoned; the recovery states that the link to the prior identity will be published within the horizon.

title: Encourage a second independent adoption early

rule.text: Encourage a second independent adoption early

given: A release build with a user holding one adoption.
when: A reviewer uses the client through its first sessions.
then: The client prompts, unobtrusively and before any eclipse condition, that a second independent adoption protects against a single patron.

title: Resolve simultaneous opposite adoptions by asking the two to choose a direction

rule.text: ask them to choose one direction rather than reporting a protocol failure

given: Two release-build clients in one ceremony each proposing to adopt the other.
when: A reviewer triggers the conflict.
then: Both clients present a choice of direction and neither reports a protocol error.

title: Disclose to operators what their subordinates are exposed to, the hosting model, and the roles users hold

rule.text: Tell an operator plainly what their subordinates are exposed to
Display whether a resource is hosted here or brokered to an external service.
The roles they hold on each resource.

given: A release build of the infra client with one hosted and one brokered resource.
when: A reviewer binds each resource and views a member's access.
then: The binding view shows hosted against brokered; the operator view states the exposure the configuration creates; the accessing user's view shows the roles held and not the predicates.

title: Encrypt backups under a key kept apart, say what losing the device costs, and scan imports for expired retention

rule.text: Encrypt under a key not stored alongside it.
Maintain backups, and make the consequence visible to the user.
Scan any imported backup for expired retention

given: A release build.
when: A reviewer creates a backup, reads the backup screen, and imports a backup containing captures past their window.
then: The backup is encrypted under a passphrase-derived key not stored with it; the screen states what device loss costs; the import deletes the expired captures and says so.

title: Tell the user on first brokered use that ending membership does not end the vendor's session

rule.text: Tell the user, when they first use a brokered resource, that ending their membership will not end that vendor's session.

given: A release build with a brokered resource available.
when: A reviewer opens the brokered resource for the first time.
then: A notice states that the vendor's session outlives membership, shown once, before traffic is routed.

title: Present a restored archive as recovered on trust, never as verified-complete

rule.text: never present a restored archive as verified-complete

given: A release build on a device that lost its archive.
when: A reviewer restores from a holder.
then: The interface states that the restored history is complete only as far as the holder claims and was not verified complete.

title: Forward a stored topology transaction on every adjacent session except the one it arrived from

rule.text: a node forwards a stored transaction to every adjacent node except the one it arrived from
forward if and only if you stored it, duplicate-suppressed by `txid`, with no hop count and no acknowledgement

given: Node N holds authenticated sessions with its patron P, subordinates S1 and S2, a peer Q and an attached client C. An adoption whose subject lies within N's own h_store, signed by keys N holds, arrives on the session from P.
when: N receives the TopologyPush carrying it.
then: N stores the transaction, and one TopologyPush frame carrying the object byte-for-byte is observed on each of the sessions to S1, S2, Q and C, and none on the session to P.

title: Forward nothing whose subject lies outside your own h_store

rule.text: A node stores a topology-class transaction when its subject falls within that node's own `h_store`
There is no hop count, no TTL and no reach field.
A horizon is every node within a two-edge walk of you

given: Node N as in PRP-01. An adoption arrives from P whose subject is three adoption edges from N and whose signatures verify.
when: N receives the TopologyPush.
then: N's store does not gain the transaction and no TopologyPush follows on any of N's sessions. Nothing in the frame told N how far to forward; the decision came from N's own store.

title: Neither store nor forward an object you already hold

rule.text: A node that already holds an object does not store it again and does not forward it.

given: Node N holds a transaction with txid T, received from P and already forwarded.
when: The same object arrives again on the session from Q.
then: N's store is unchanged and no TopologyPush carrying T is observed on any session after the second arrival.

title: Hold a transaction whose signer key you lack, and forward it once it verifies

rule.text: Stored means verified.
hold it, fetch the key, and let it enter storage and propagation when it verifies

given: Node N as in PRP-01. An adoption arrives whose subject is within h_store but one of whose signers' KeyMaterial N does not hold.
when: N receives the TopologyPush, and the missing KeyMaterial is later supplied through the path N uses to fetch it.
then: No TopologyPush carrying the object is observed on any session before the key arrives. After the key arrives and every signature verifies, the object is in N's store and a TopologyPush carrying it is observed on the sessions PRP-01 names.

title: Relay a stored object you are not a party to

rule.text: This governs origination, not relaying.
a relay changes nothing

given: Node N is neither the patron nor the subject of an adoption that lies within its h_store; it arrived from P.
when: N receives the TopologyPush.
then: N forwards it as PRP-01 describes. An implementation that applies the who-may-push rule to relays, forwarding only objects it is a party to, stops the flood here and fails.

title: Carry a pushed object byte-for-byte with a body-kind tag and nothing else

rule.text: carrying the object byte-for-byte with a body-kind tag and nothing else
That is the only wrapper field permitted.

given: Node N receives a TopologyPush from P whose object bytes are recorded by the test.
when: N forwards it to S1.
then: The frame observed on the session to S1 carries an object whose bytes equal the recorded bytes exactly, and a wrapper carrying the body-kind tag and no other field.

title: Let a later EndpointRecord supersede the held one and a lower or equal seqno die as a duplicate

rule.text: An `EndpointRecord` therefore supersedes rather than accumulating
the held `seqno` is greater than or equal (§2.3)

given: Node N holds subject X's EndpointRecord at seqno 5 in the series it has proved current.
when: A record for X at seqno 4, then an identical record at seqno 5, then a validly signed record at seqno 6 in the same series arrive in turn.
then: After the first two arrivals N's current record for X is still the seqno 5 record and no TopologyPush follows. After the third, N's current record for X is the seqno 6 record and one TopologyPush carrying it is observed on each adjacent session except the one it arrived from.

title: Retain neither of two different signed contents at one seqno, forward nothing for that pair, and re-resolve

rule.text: Equal `seqno` with different signed contents is malformed
a holder retains neither as current and forwards nothing further for that `(subject, seqno)`
it repairs by re-resolving (§7.7)

given: Node N holds X's EndpointRecord at seqno 5 with contents A, already forwarded.
when: A validly signed EndpointRecord for X at seqno 5 with different contents B arrives.
then: N holds no current record for X, no TopologyPush carrying either record is observed after the conflict, and a resolution for X is observed leaving N.

title: Drop a memo whose anchor is not your subnet's

rule.text: So a memo whose anchor is not your subnet's is dropped, not forwarded
neither applied to a table nor passed on
A memo never leaves its subnet.

given: Node N sits in the subnet anchored at A, with patron P, and keeps a memo table.
when: A TopologyMemo whose anchor is B arrives from a subordinate.
then: No TopologyMemo is observed on N's session to P and N's memo table is unchanged.

title: Forward a memo unchanged to your patron, and stop at the root

rule.text: A receiving node forwards the memo to its own patron, unchanged except that nothing is added
A root has no patron and forwarding stops there.

given: Node N with patron P, and root R with no patron, each receive a memo from a subordinate about a slot neither holds.
when: Each processes the memo.
then: On N's session to P a TopologyMemo is observed whose bytes equal the received memo's. R sends no TopologyMemo on any session.

title: Forward no memo about a slot you hold at or after its timestamp

rule.text: A node holding that slot at or after the memo's timestamp does not forward it.

given: Node N with patron P holds subordinate slot k with an occupant and a timestamp t.
when: A memo naming N in field 1 and slot k, with field 4 at or before t, arrives from below.
then: No TopologyMemo is observed on N's session to P.

title: Treat a memo naming you as a cycle, confirm it against your own row, and disavow the subordinate that forwarded it

rule.text: If field 1 is you, a memo you originated has come back to you from below
It fires at any depth, on the memo alone, and terminates the memo there.
It disavows the direct subordinate that forwarded the memo to it
Reason code 5, without prejudice

given: Node N holds subordinate S in slot k and a row matching that. A cycle below S has formed, so a memo N originated for slot k returns to N on the session from S.
when: N receives the memo.
then: No TopologyMemo is forwarded further. A disavowal transaction by N naming S with reason code 5 is observed, and N's slot k is empty afterwards.

title: Act on no memo your own records do not confirm

rule.text: No node acts on a memo alone.
A fabricated memo fails both, at no traffic cost.

given: Node N holds subordinate S in slot k. An attacker below S injects a memo naming N in field 1 and slot k but naming an occupant N's row does not hold.
when: N receives the memo from S.
then: No disavowal is emitted, no archive fetch is issued, the memo is not forwarded, and N's rows are unchanged.
