title: Send a memo to the nearest infrastructure node when the patron holds no session

rule.text: Where no session with the patron exists, the memo goes to the nearest infrastructure node on the patron chain instead

given: Node N's patron L is a light client that holds no sessions; N's serving node I is the nearest infrastructure node on the patron chain.
when: N adopts a subordinate and originates the corresponding memo.
then: The TopologyMemo is observed on N's session to I, and nothing is attempted toward L.

title: Repair a missed object by reconciliation that replays the same frame

rule.text: reconciliation is a replay of the same frames rather than a distinct mechanism
Loss is detected at the receiver, which is the party that can act.

given: An adoption within N's h_store was lost in flight, so N holds neither it nor a later object that back-points to it. The test triggers reconciliation between N and its patron, since when it runs is local.
when: N reconciles.
then: The missing object arrives at N as a TopologyPush frame of the same shape as the original, N stores it, and forwards it as PRP-01 describes.

title: Send a memo down the branch holding the slot the arriving memo did not name

rule.text: sends a memo down the branch holding the slot the arriving memo did not name
Nothing compels the receiving patron to act.
a node appearing in two slots is held in two places

given: Node N keeps a memo table holding occupant O under patron S1's slot from an earlier memo. A memo from S2, another subordinate of N, places O in S2's slot at a later timestamp.
when: N receives S2's memo, and S1 then receives what N sent it.
then: N forwards the memo rootward and sends the same frame down the branch toward S1, not back toward S2. S1 reports the occupant held elsewhere, keeps its own row, and sends nothing on. A node handed the memo from above with the earlier row in its table walks it down and does not turn it round.

title: Keep no memo table, and still forward every memo

rule.text: The table is optional, and detection degrades gracefully rather than failing.
No tier is load-bearing.

given: Node N keeps no memo table. Two memos from two subordinates place the same occupant in two slots.
when: N receives both.
then: Both are forwarded rootward unchanged, no downward memo is sent, and the same memo arriving from above finds nothing to walk down. An implementation that requires the table fails.

title: Confirm a cycle memo about an emptied slot by the empty row

rule.text: An empty slot is a row, not a deletion.
once the memo is confirmed against its own records

given: Node N emptied its slot k at time t. N's own memo for slot k, with no occupant, returns from a subordinate.
when: N receives it.
then: N confirms the cycle against its empty row and disavows the forwarding subordinate with reason code 5. A memo about a slot N never held a row for is not confirmed and nothing is sent.

title: Queue messages for a client that is not attached, and report the count at its next attach.

rule.text: Undelivered messages queue indefinitely at the recipient's serving node
messages queued for this client AT THE RESPONDING NODE
Hold ciphertext for offline clients

given: N is patron and serving node of light client C; C is not attached. Sender X submits k ciphertext messages addressed to C's keyhash to N, and N accepts each.
when: C attaches to N.
then: N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to k.
interpretation: The payload submission path by which a sender hands a message for C to N has no wire encoding (design §14.2.4's integration decisions are open); the test uses the implementation's own and observes the queue through AttachAck field 4 and the drain streams.

title: Deliver queued ciphertext, unchanged, when the client returns.

rule.text: The message waits; it is not lost.
Unidirectional streams: payload delivery, queue drain
The recipient's serving node holds ciphertext until reconnect

given: k messages are queued at N for C, each a distinct ciphertext the harness recorded at submission.
when: C attaches to N and reads its unidirectional streams.
then: C receives k drain deliveries, and the set of ciphertexts received equals the set submitted, byte for byte.

title: Delete on delivery: a second attach finds nothing and redelivers nothing.

rule.text: No copy outlives delivery. Deletion on delivery is immediate and leaves nothing recoverable — no journal, no tombstone.
Delete on delivery, immediately, leaving nothing recoverable.
messages queued for this client AT THE RESPONDING NODE

given: k messages were queued at N for C; C attached and received all k on drain streams, then closed the session.
when: C attaches to N again.
then: N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 0 and no drain delivery follows; N's inspectable queue store holds no copy of any of the k ciphertexts.

title: Keep no crash-recovery copy that outlives a delivery.

rule.text: No journal, no tombstone, no crash-recovery copy that outlives the delete. Durable storage for your own crash recovery is your backup problem and must not extend a message's life.
No copy outlives delivery.

given: k messages were queued at N for C; C attached and received all k, then closed the session.
when: N's process is killed without warning and restarted from whatever it persisted; C attaches to N again.
then: N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 0, no drain delivery follows, and none of the k ciphertexts is present in N's storage after the restart.

title: Hold only ciphertext, recipient keyhash and arrival time while a message waits.

rule.text: Hold the minimum while a message waits: ciphertext, recipient keyhash, arrival time. Nothing further.
Queue metadata is the minimum: ciphertext, recipient keyhash, arrival time.

given: Sender X submitted one message addressed to C to N while C was not attached, and N accepted it; N exposes its queue store to the test.
when: The test inspects N's record of the waiting message.
then: The record consists of the ciphertext, C's keyhash and an arrival time, and carries nothing further: in particular no identity or address of X.

title: Refuse the newest message at the cap and tell the sender; keep what is queued.

rule.text: At the ceiling: refuse the newest message and tell the sender. Never drop the oldest.
At the cap, refuse the newest message and tell the sender

given: The queue cap is unset (design §21.1) and is a test parameter: N is configured with a per-subordinate storage cap sized so that exactly k test messages for one subordinate fit. C is not attached; X has submitted k messages for C and N accepted each.
when: X submits a (k+1)th message addressed to C.
then: X receives a refusal for the (k+1)th message, distinguishable from acceptance; at C's next attach field 4 equals k and the k earlier ciphertexts are all delivered.
interpretation: The sender-facing refusal has no wire encoding; the test checks only that X receives a refusal for that message that differs from the acceptance the earlier k received.

title: Let no flood displace what is already queued.

rule.text: Never drop the oldest: it destroys a message the sender believes was accepted, and it lets anyone who can reach the queue flush what is already in it.
Refuse-newest bounds an attacker to denying new delivery, which the sender sees.

given: The queue cap is unset (design §21.1) and is a test parameter: N is configured with a per-subordinate storage cap sized so that exactly k test messages for one subordinate fit. C is not attached; k legitimate messages for C are queued and N is at C's cap.
when: An attacker A submits several times k further messages addressed to C in quick succession, then C attaches.
then: Every one of A's messages is refused to A; C's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to k and the k legitimate ciphertexts are all delivered, none replaced by A's.
interpretation: The sender-facing refusal has no wire encoding; the test checks only that A receives a refusal for each message.

title: Keep a queued message across an absence of any length.

rule.text: No time limit: a message survives an absence of any length.
No time limit; a space limit.

given: One message is queued at N for C, who is not attached. The absence length is a test parameter: the harness advances N's clock by a chosen long duration D and lets N run on.
when: After D, C attaches to N.
then: N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 1 and the message is delivered on a drain stream.

title: Apply the cap per subordinate, so one full queue does not refuse another's mail.

rule.text: Undelivered messages queue indefinitely at the recipient's serving node
Queue indefinitely, bounded by a per-subordinate storage cap

given: The queue cap is unset (design §21.1) and is a test parameter: N is configured with a per-subordinate storage cap sized so that exactly k test messages for one subordinate fit. N serves C1 and C2, neither attached; C1's queue holds k messages and is at its cap.
when: X submits one message addressed to C2, then C2 attaches.
then: N accepts the message for C2, and C2's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 1 with the message delivered on a drain stream.

title: Queue for a client the node has marked unreachable, and deliver at its fresh attach.

rule.text: the serving node marks the client unreachable; material for it queues as it always did, and delivery waits for its return.
Hold ciphertext for offline clients
The message waits; it is not lost.

given: C is attached to N with a heartbeat interval I (unset, design §21.1; a test parameter). The harness blackholes all packets between C and N for three full intervals so that N marks C unreachable.
when: X submits one message addressed to C; the blackhole is lifted and C performs a fresh attach to N.
then: N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 1 and the message is delivered on a drain stream.
interpretation: Whether N ends the old session on marking C unreachable is not stated; the test has C attach afresh and does not depend on the old session's fate.

title: Distinguish an offline subordinate from a keyhash with no record.

rule.text: §7.4.3's queue mechanism depends on the node distinguishing "offline" from "no record"
Queries to an offline light client queue at its patron, resolving when the client next connects

given: N serves C, who is not attached, and holds no record of keyhash Z, which belongs to no node in N's topology.
when: X submits one message addressed to C and one addressed to Z.
then: The message for C is queued (C's next AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 1); nothing is queued for Z in N's inspectable store, and the answer X receives for Z differs from the one it received for C.
interpretation: Neither the acceptance nor the no-record answer to the sender has a wire encoding; the test checks only that the two answers are distinguishable to X.

title: Report no queued messages from a failover sibling, which holds no queue state.

rule.text: Do not replicate queue state to siblings.
Siblings do not hold queue state.
messages queued for this client AT THE RESPONDING NODE

given: N and S are siblings; k messages are queued at N for C; nothing addressed to C was ever submitted to S. C is attached to N with interval I (a test parameter) and holds S's SiblingRef with KeyMaterial.
when: N goes dark; after three missed intervals C attaches to S.
then: S's AttachAck carries field 1 equal to 1 and field 4 equal to 0, and S delivers nothing on drain streams.

title: Collect from the patron, in full, once it returns after a failover.

rule.text: a client attached to a sibling still collects from its own serving node once that node returns
a client attached to a sibling collects from its own serving node when that node returns

given: k messages are queued at N for C; N went dark and C holds a degraded session on sibling S.
when: N returns; C's session on S ends and C performs a fresh attach.
then: C attaches to N, N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to k, and all k ciphertexts are delivered on drain streams.

title: End a running session once the node holds supersession evidence for its credential.

rule.text: sessions under the superseded credential terminate, and nothing further is delivered to it, queued material and capture-key grants included.
Terminate its sessions and deliver nothing further to it, its queue included.

given: C is attached to N under keyhash K_old with a live session.
when: N takes authenticated supersession evidence for C's binding: a verified reissue chain onto a new series, or a recovery it has validated.
then: N closes C's connection, and no payload or drain delivery reaches that session after the evidence was taken.
interpretation: No close code is assigned for ending a session on supersession; the test checks that the connection is closed by N and not which code it carries.

title: Deliver nothing queued to a credential the node has verified superseded.

rule.text: sessions under the superseded credential terminate, and nothing further is delivered to it, queued material and capture-key grants included.
Stop serving a binding you have verified superseded

given: k messages are queued at N for keyhash K_old; N has since taken authenticated supersession evidence for that binding (a verified reissue chain onto a new series, or a validated recovery).
when: A client presenting K_old dials N and sends Attach.
then: N sends no AttachAck and no drain delivery on that connection.
interpretation: Whether the attach is closed with application close code 1 or otherwise is not assigned; the test checks only that no AttachAck and no delivery follow.

title: Hand nothing queued for a superseded keyhash to its successor.

rule.text: Queue metadata is the minimum: ciphertext, recipient keyhash, arrival time.
nothing further is delivered to it, queued material and capture-key grants included.

given: k messages are queued at N for keyhash K_old; N has taken authenticated supersession evidence moving that binding to K_new, and nothing addressed to K_new has been submitted.
when: A client presenting K_new attaches to N.
then: N's AttachAck carries field 4 equal to 0 and no drain delivery carries any of the k ciphertexts.
interpretation: That delivery is keyed by the queued recipient keyhash is the model's reading (tamarin/compliant/attach); the specification says nothing further goes to the superseded credential and does not say whether a successor collects material queued for its predecessor.

title: Assemble a recovery adoption carrying both halves and no other evidence field

rule.text: A recovery requires both, always: the old key and a present human.
EXACTLY ONE of fields 6, 8 and 9 is present
with `external_aad = "rhtn/1:successor"`

given: Subject S holds prior key k1 and new key k2, meets prior counterparty V who recognises S, and is re-adopted by patron P.
when: S's client assembles the adoption.
then: The adoption carries field 6 and neither field 8 nor field 9; field 6's responses are sorted ascending by verifier keyhash and include a `match`; field 6's field 3 is a hybrid COSE_Sign by k1 over the successor statement naming k1, k2 and P under the successor tag, and the corpus validator accepts the envelope.

title: Reject a recovery whose successor statement names a different successor or patron

rule.text: A verifier MUST check `new_key` and `patron_key` against adoption fields 1 and 2 and reject on mismatch.

given: Patron P receives a recovery adoption whose field 3 successor statement was lifted from another recovery and names a different new key, then one naming a different patron.
when: P evaluates each.
then: P countersigns neither and records no binding for either.

title: Sign a recovery verifier response with both components, and the consent classically

rule.text: A verifier's authentication inside a `Recovery` block is HYBRID
Field 7 stays classical

given: Verifier V answering in a recovery ceremony for subject S.
when: V's client signs its response.
then: The response's field 9 is a detached COSE_Sign with one Ed25519 and one ML-DSA-65 entry that both verify under V, and field 7 is a single classical COSE_Sign1 by S's new key.

title: Run the recovery meeting as a ceremony in which the verifier is its own querier

rule.text: The querier is the verifier
`selection_basis` MUST be 0 (met) in every response here
the counterparty is its own querier

given: Subject S stands before prior counterparty V with S's new key on the harness.
when: The recovery ceremony runs.
then: V's client generates the VerificationQuery with field 2 naming V and the meeting's own pre-commitment, S's new key countersigns it, and V's response carries selection basis 0 and field 8 equal to S's prior key.

title: Seal every old line as the old key's last act before publishing a rotation

rule.text: Seal the old line as the old key's last act.
as the last thing the old key does
sets the counter it is leaving to the maximum, then reissues naming that value

given: Subject S with prior key k1 holds series in two patron relationships and rotates to k2.
when: S's client performs the rotation.
then: Before the adoption under k2 is pushed, a self-signed SignedLocator by k1 at the maximum counter is produced for each of the two series, and nothing signed by k1 follows them.

title: On suspected compromise, seal, then reissue naming the sealed counter, for every relationship

rule.text: On suspected key compromise, seal before you take a series reissue.
Seal, then reissue, then repeat for every other patron relationship whose line is worth securing.

given: Subject S holds two patron relationships and marks its key as suspected compromised.
when: S's client acts on the suspicion.
then: For each relationship, in order, a self-signed locator at the maximum counter is produced, then a type-7 reissue whose field 3 equals that maximum and whose field 4 is a fresh series at counter 0, countersigned by that patron.

title: Never reissue into a series you have occupied

rule.text: Never take a series reissue into a series you have occupied before.
The new series MUST NOT be one the node has previously occupied.

given: Subject S has occupied series s1 then s2 and is now in s3.
when: S's client is asked to produce a reissue whose field 4 names s1 or s2.
then: No such reissue is produced; a reissue into an unused series is.

title: Reject a reissue naming a series already in the chain you hold

rule.text: who MUST reject a reissue naming a series already in it
Chain length is the order.

given: Holder H has the chain for S: adoption into s1, reissue to s2.
when: A patron-countersigned reissue for S with field 4 equal to s1 arrives, then one into an unused s3.
then: The first is rejected and H's chain is unchanged; the second extends H's chain to length three.

title: Reject records in an abandoned series whatever their counter

rule.text: MUST reject records in it whatever their counter

given: Holder H has S's chain showing s1 left for s2.
when: A validly signed locator for S in s1 at a counter above every s1 record H holds arrives, then a locator in s2 at counter 1.
then: The s1 locator is rejected; the s2 locator is installed.

title: Present the chain when asked to rank, and never propagate it

rule.text: Keep the chain that proves your current series
It is presented, never propagated
Presentation, not propagation, and not a history scan.

given: Subject S holds its adoption and one reissue; a counterparty asks S to prove its series.
when: S answers, and the test watches S's sessions for a period afterwards.
then: The adoption and the reissue are presented to the counterparty; no TopologyPush carrying either leaves S in response.

title: Let a thief's seal freeze a chainless holder's entry, and never move it afterwards

rule.text: against them it is a race the thief can win by reaching a reader first
What a recipient ends up holding is an address that can never be updated.
So a thief who seals first burns a line rather than capturing one.

given: Holder H has a cached locator for S in series s at counter 5 and no chain. A thief holding S's key produces a locator in s at the maximum counter.
when: The thief's locator reaches H first; S's locator in s at counter 6 arrives later.
then: H installs the thief's locator, rejects S's counter-6 locator, and no further record in s changes H's entry.

title: Resolve two competing recoveries for one prior key to one current binding, by trusted patron

rule.text: it resolves to one, by which patron it trusts
Both successors remain valid nodes network-wide

given: Observer O within the horizon receives two recovery adoptions for prior key k1: successor kX under patron X and successor kY under patron Y, with O's policy set by the test to prefer X.
when: O processes both.
then: O's binding for the identity is kX alone; kY is held as a distinct valid node and not as the continuation.
interpretation: Which patron an observer trusts is policy; the test fixes it and asserts that exactly one continuation results.

title: Carry nothing in a plain rotation

rule.text: A plain rotation carries nothing
A plain rotation carries nothing

given: Subject S rotates from k1 to k2 without claiming k1's history.
when: S's client performs the rotation and the memo for the adoption travels rootward.
then: The adoption carries no field 6, no field naming k1 anywhere, and the memo carries no prior key.

title: Reject a transfer whose statement disagrees with the enclosing adoption

rule.text: A verifier MUST check all three against the enclosing adoption

given: Patron P receives a transfer adoption whose TransferStatement names a different node, then one naming a different new patron, then one naming a different former patron than the Transfer map's field 1.
when: P evaluates each.
then: P countersigns none of them.

title: Replicate a client's unreachable marking to the serving node's siblings

rule.text: This state replicates to siblings, or a sibling answering during failover has no idea of the client's status.
Siblings replicate each other's topology and trust-bearing transaction history (up to f−1 = 9).

given: Infra nodes S and T are siblings under one patron; light client L is attached to S. No separate replication agreement exists between S and T beyond the patron's adoption transactions.
when: L's heartbeat fails at S, S marks L unreachable, and L is then attached to T in failover.
then: T's reachability state for L shows L as unreachable-and-queuing rather than as unknown; T does not answer for L as if it held no record of L.
interpretation: No wire frame is specified as the carrier of this replicated state; the test observes T's resulting state only and leaves the carrier to the implementation.

title: Do not replicate queue state to siblings

rule.text: Do not replicate queue state to siblings.
Siblings do not hold queue state.

given: Sibling infra nodes S and T; light client L attached to S is marked unreachable at S, and three messages for L are queued at S.
when: L attaches to T in failover and collects.
then: T delivers none of the three messages, T's store holds no queued ciphertext for L, and T's AttachAck field 4 does not count S's mailbox.

title: Issue secondhand from replicated state while the patron is dark

rule.text: A sibling issues a fresh attestation reflecting whatever rotation reached the replicated state.
a consumer must be able to weight a secondhand attestation lower

given: Infra patron P adopted L; sibling T holds P's replicated adoption records for L. P then countersigns a rotation for L that has not yet reached T. P becomes unreachable.
when: A currency request for L is sent to T.
then: T returns a CurrencyAttestation whose field 5 is 1 and whose field 2 is the key T's replicated state holds for L; the reply carries no indication that P's state differs, so the lag is visible only as the secondhand role.
interpretation: The spec does not name replication lag; the test reads 'whatever rotation reached the replicated state' as: the sibling attests what it holds and neither fetches from the dark patron nor marks its state as behind.

title: Accept a move within the replication horizon without archive presentation

rule.text: Implementations MUST NOT force re-verification in this case.

it already holds the node's history through
sibling replication (design §3.4), so **no archive presentation or re-verification is
needed and trust history is preserved**

given: Light client L is adopted under infra node P; T is P's sibling and holds L's history through sibling replication.
when: L presents T an adoption carrying P's countersignature (a lateral shift) with no archive presentation.
then: T completes the adoption; no archive-fetch request and no presence ceremony are required of L.
interpretation: 'No archive presentation or re-verification' is observed as the absence of an archive-fetch request and of a presence-ceremony requirement; the spec names no other observable.

title: Accept a peering record whose self-asserted ASN is not validated against its address

rule.text: The field is optional and self-asserted besides — no IP-to-ASN validation is specified anywhere.

given: A well-formed peering transaction between infra nodes A and B, each NetworkPoint carrying an ASN that does not correspond to its IPv4 address in any public routing data.
when: A node in A's horizon receives the record by topology push.
then: The record is accepted and stored, and the ASN values it exposes are exactly those asserted; no validation failure is reported.

title: Expose both peers' addresses and ASNs from a stored peering record

rule.text: The record carries each endpoint's network point. Address, and where available the ASN, so concentration is observable rather than asserted
The peering record carries the ASN for both endpoints

given: Infra nodes A and B, in different subtrees and both carrying ASNs, have peered; observer O is in A's horizon and has stored the peering record.
when: O's client reads A's peering relationships.
then: The stored record yields A's and B's keyhashes, both IPv4 addresses and both ASNs as decoded from the record's NetworkPoints, with nothing withheld or derived.

title: Leave the trust metric's output unchanged by ASN concentration

rule.text: Concentration is a visible signal, not a trust input — nothing in the metric consumes it.

given: Two otherwise identical fixed graphs, differing only in that in one every peering NetworkPoint carries the same ASN and in the other every ASN differs.
when: The reference metric scores the same target from the same observer in each graph.
then: The two scores are identical.

title: Generate no rootward memo for a peering record

rule.text: Peering is topology class and is excluded from rootward travel

given: Infra node A, with patron P, grandpatron G and root R above it, peers with infra node B in another subtree.
when: A pushes the peering record into its horizon.
then: No TopologyMemo derived from the peering is sent to P, and neither G's nor R's memo table gains an entry naming B's NetworkPoint or ASN.

title: Make an infra node's peerlessness observable from held topology

rule.text: Peering transactions are public, so this is observable
trust policies should discount peerless infra nodes, and the reference client should tell an operator plainly what their subordinates are exposed to

given: Observer O's horizon contains infra nodes I and J; J has one peering record stored at O and I has none.
when: O's client enumerates cross-tree peers for I and for J.
then: I is reported with zero peers and J with one, both derived from O's own topology store, and I's zero is surfaced to the user rather than omitted.
interpretation: 'Should tell an operator plainly' is a reference-client commitment; the test asserts only that the count is derivable and displayed, and leaves any policy discount unspecified.

title: Adopt with zero peers

rule.text: a disconnected node must be able to adopt or be adopted before it has any peers
zero peers is a supported configuration

given: Infra node I is a root with no peering records and no patron; node N holds a proof of presence with I.
when: I adopts N.
then: The adoption completes and is stored; no step refuses or defers it for want of a peering record.

title: Take the direct payload path inside the horizon

rule.text: Direct | Peer is inside the horizon (§15.1), both online, traversal succeeds | Nobody. The peers exchange addresses during setup and connect
"Is this peer in my h=2 topology store?" is the entire check.

given: Light clients L1 and L2 are siblings (distance 1, inside each other's h=2 horizon), both online and attached, with a NAT traversal that succeeds; no user override is set.
when: L1 sends payload to L2.
then: L2 receives the payload directly from L1's address; neither serving node carries the payload bytes.

title: Relay, never connect directly, to a peer outside the horizon

rule.text: Direct connection is limited to the horizon, because a direct path reveals each peer's IP to the other (P17).
Relayed | Peer is outside the horizon, or traversal fails — symmetric NAT, CGNAT, two mobile peers | Both serving infra nodes, as TURN relays carrying ciphertext

given: Light clients L1 (serving node S1) and L2 (serving node S2) sit in different subtrees, outside each other's h=2 horizon; both online; no user override.
when: L1 sends payload to L2.
then: The payload passes through S1 and S2 as ciphertext; L1 opens no connection to L2's address, and L2 learns no address for L1.

title: Do not count a peering edge toward the horizon for the direct path

rule.text: It confers no scope, and does not extend the horizon.
Peering edges do not count (§6.3): a peering edge is ungoverned and carries none of the subnet's authority, so it contributes flow without conferring scope.

given: Infra nodes A and B, in different subtrees, have peered. Light client L attaches to A and light client M to B; without the peering edge they are outside each other's horizon; both online; no override.
when: L sends payload to M.
then: The payload is relayed through A and B; M is absent from L's h=2 topology store and no direct connection is attempted.

title: Honour a user override of the direct-path default

rule.text: both defaults must therefore be overridable — relay-with-a-patron's-sibling and direct-with-a-distant-trusted-party are both reasonable user choices (P17)

given: As REP-12 (L1 and L2 outside each other's horizon), except that L1's user has chosen direct connection for L2 and L2's user has chosen it for L1; traversal succeeds.
when: L1 sends payload to L2.
then: L2 receives the payload directly from L1's address and neither serving node carries it.
interpretation: The spec makes the default overridable and does not say whether one side's choice suffices; the test sets the override on both sides.

title: Push the serving node's siblings, not the patron's, as the replication set

rule.text: siblings of the serving node, not of the patron, where those differ

given: Light client L's patron P is a light client under infra node S; S has infra siblings T1 and T2; P has light-client sibling Q.
when: L attaches to S.
then: The AttachAck's SiblingRef list names T1 and T2 with their endpoints, and does not name Q.

title: Replicate topology and trust-bearing history to siblings, and no queue state

rule.text: every user's topology and trust-bearing transaction history replicates on their nearest infra node and that node's siblings
Payload queues do not replicate
Siblings do not hold queue state.

given: Infra node N with sibling N', an attached client C with an adoption and a presence record in N's store, and a message queued for C at N.
when: Replication runs and the test inspects N'.
then: N' holds C's adoption and presence record; N' holds no queued message for C and no record that one is waiting.

title: Use a gossiped anchor entry as a starting point without authenticating the anchor

rule.text: Full keys are not fetched during resolution — they arrive from attaching, from a transaction naming the node, or not at all
an anchor that refers you onward is never pinned at all

given: The node's anchor table holds an AnchorEntry for anchor A received by gossip: A's keyhash, one to eight NetworkPoints, subtree size, seqno and A's self-signature. The node holds no KeyMaterial for A and has never contacted A.
when: The node resolves a SignedLocator whose anchor is A and whose path leads to a subject beneath A.
then: A ResolveRequest is sent to an endpoint taken from the entry; the ResolveReply's Referral is followed to the next hop; at no point is A's key material fetched or a pin for A created, and the resolution still completes at the serving node.

title: Retain anchor entries only at or above the node's own caching threshold

rule.text: each node sets its own threshold for which roots it caches. For example, ignoring roots with fewer than n subordinates
Which anchors a node caches is per-node policy, never a protocol constant.

given: The anchor caching threshold n is a parameter of the test, since design §21.1 leaves it unset; the node under test is configured with a chosen n. Two well-formed AnchorEntry objects arrive by gossip for roots R1 and R2, with subtree sizes n−1 and n.
when: The node ingests both entries.
then: R2's entry is present in the anchor table and R1's is not; a locator anchored at R1 is reported unresolvable by this node while one anchored at R2 proceeds to a ResolveRequest.
interpretation: The quantity compared against n is AnchorEntry field 3 (subtree size), which the test reads as design §12.7.3's count of subordinates.

title: Send no request for a locator whose anchor is absent from the table

rule.text: A locator whose anchor is absent from the local table is not resolvable by this node. That is a caller-side condition, not a wire failure: no request is sent, because there is nowhere to send it.

given: The node's anchor table holds no entry for anchor A, and no other source (an introduction, a cached entry, a peer's referral) has supplied an address for A.
when: The node is asked to resolve a valid SignedLocator anchored at A.
then: No ResolveRequest is emitted on any connection; the resolution result is reported as a caller-side condition distinct from every wire failure code.

title: Accept a same-series counter jump as a valid supersession

rule.text: Within one series a new counter must be strictly greater than the last one the verifier holds — not exactly previous+1, since a verifier may legitimately have missed intervening transactions

given: The holder has installed the primitives.md SignedLocator for alice with seqno [5, 42] as her current locator.
when: The primitives.md 'Same-series counter jump' SignedLocator for alice, seqno [5, 100], is presented.
then: The [5, 100] locator is accepted and becomes the held locator for alice; the [5, 42] locator is no longer reported as current.

title: Retain neither locator when equal seqnos carry different contents

rule.text: malformed names the pair, the holder retains neither as current and re-resolves — kept-because-it-arrived-first is not a freshness rule

given: The holder has installed alice's [5, 100] counter-jump SignedLocator from primitives.md. Its conflict partner (V12), same subject, same [5, 100], different path, is validly signed.
when: The conflict partner is presented and the holder is then asked to reach alice.
then: Neither locator is reported as alice's current locator, and the attempt to reach her produces a re-resolution rather than a dial to either path.
interpretation: 'Re-resolves' is observed as the holder declining to dial either path and signalling that a fresh locator is required; the spec places the fresh locator's source in design §12.3 Case 3 or §12.4, outside this test.

title: Do not rank two locators for one subject that lie in different series

rule.text: Across series there is no order, and a reader MUST NOT invent one.
Two locators in different series do not rank, and a reader holding both has learned nothing about which is current — it either holds a §4.6 chain that says, or it re-resolves

given: The holder has alice's [5, 100] SignedLocator installed and holds no series-reissue chain for her.
when: A validly signed SignedLocator for alice with seqno [9, 3] and a different path is presented.
then: The [9, 3] locator is not installed as fresher and the [5, 100] locator is not marked stale; the holder reports that it cannot determine which is current.
interpretation: The spec says the reader 'has learned nothing'; the test reads this as the held locator left unchanged, the newcomer not installed, and the reader signalling indeterminacy rather than choosing.

title: Route a light client's resolution through its serving node

rule.text: A light client sends ResolveRequest to its serving infra node, not to the anchor.
The serving node resolves on the client's behalf and returns the result.

given: Light client L is attached to serving node S. L holds a SignedLocator for subject X anchored at A; S holds an anchor entry for A and L holds none.
when: L resolves X.
then: L's only ResolveRequest is sent on its session with S; S sends a ResolveRequest to an endpoint of A and follows any referrals; L receives X's serving node and residual path from S and opens no connection to A.

title: Answer authoritatively with the residual suffix for a client attached past a light-client patron

rule.text: The remaining path suffix is returned rather than traversed. The serving node uses it to identify which of its attached clients is meant.
You resolve their paths yourself; nothing routes through an intermediate light-client patron.

given: Infra node S has light-client subordinate P, and P has adopted light client L, so L attaches to S at depth two beneath it.
when: S receives a ResolveRequest naming L, with the anchor and full anchor-relative path to L.
then: The reply has field 2 = 0 and a ServingInfra whose field 1 is S's keyhash and whose path field is the non-empty suffix identifying L beneath S; no request is forwarded to P.

title: Resolve a root's self-anchored locator to an empty residual path

rule.text: empty means the addressed party is the node itself, non-empty means the last hop forwards to an attached client
a root names itself, with an empty path

given: Root R is an infra node; the requester holds an anchor entry for R and R's self-anchored SignedLocator from primitives.md (anchor = R, empty path).
when: The requester sends R a ResolveRequest with subject R, anchor R and the empty path.
then: The reply has field 2 = 0 and a ServingInfra naming R with an empty path field, and the requester treats R itself as the addressed party.

title: Refer from an infra child's endpoint record before ever contacting the child

rule.text: Unverified does not mean unusable: refer from it.
Refer when it does not: the next hop's keyhash, its endpoints, and its KeyMaterial where the requester may lack it.

given: Infra node S adopted infra node C. S has received C's EndpointRecord by topology push, holds no KeyMaterial for C and has never dialled C.
when: S receives a ResolveRequest whose path leads into C's subtree.
then: The reply has field 2 = 2 and a Referral whose field 1 is C's keyhash, whose field 2 is the endpoint list from C's record, and whose field 3 is at least 1; S opens no connection to C before replying.

title: Reject a referral that advances nothing

rule.text: advances MUST be ≥ 1, and a referral advancing past the path's end is malformed

given: A requester is mid-resolution, having sent a ResolveRequest with a three-index path to node N.
when: N replies with field 2 = 2 and a Referral whose field 3 is 0.
then: The named next hop is not dialled and the reply is rejected as malformed.
interpretation: What the requester does after rejecting a malformed reply (retry at another endpoint of N, or report failure) is not stated; the test asserts only that the loop is not followed.

title: Fail the handshake, not the identity, when an unsigned reply gives a wrong address

rule.text: The reply is not signed.
The dialling party checks that key is the classical member of the KeyMaterial it has pinned for the keyhash it intended to reach.
A wrong or hostile reply causes a failed connection, not a false identity.

given: The requester intends to reach subject X, whose serving node is S, and holds S's KeyMaterial pinned. A ResolveReply names S's keyhash in ServingInfra but lists the endpoint of a different node Y, which presents Y's own key.
when: The requester dials the listed endpoint.
then: The handshake fails because the presented key is not the classical member of S's pinned KeyMaterial; no session, Attach or payload follows, and the result is reported as a failed contact with S, never as having reached S.

title: Try the remaining serving endpoints when the first fails

rule.text: an implementation MUST treat the list as ; alternatives and try others on failure, or a ; single unreachable first entry becomes a ; permanent outage for that peer

given: A ServingInfra reply lists two NetworkPoints for serving node S in preference order; the first does not respond, the second is live and presents S's key.
when: The requester contacts S.
then: After the first endpoint fails the second is dialled, the handshake completes against S's pinned key, and the contact is reported as successful.

title: Remove a departed infra child and fail, never redirect, for its old path

rule.text: Remove a child on departure or disavowal. A stale entry refers requesters to a node that will not answer for that path.
Keep nothing for a node that has left your subtree, and do not redirect on its behalf.

given: Infra node S holds a child-table entry for infra child C at index i. C then departs (a departure transaction S stores) and is adopted by an unrelated patron, whose position S also learns from topology.
when: S receives a ResolveRequest whose path passes through index i beneath S.
then: The reply has field 2 = 1 with failure code 0 or 1; no Referral naming C or C's new position is returned, and S's child table no longer lists C.
interpretation: The spec requires failure rather than referral and names codes 0 and 1 as the stale-locator outcomes; which of the two S returns is the test's reading, and either is accepted.

title: Replace an infra child's endpoint list on a strictly greater counter, reordering included

rule.text: Publishing a changed endpoint list advances the counter — and the list is ordered, so reordering alone is a change
Freshness by seqno, strictly greater counter to replace within a series

given: Infra node S holds infra child C's EndpointRecord with seqno [s, c] listing endpoints [E1, E2].
when: C publishes a record with seqno [s, c+1] listing [E2, E1], and S then receives a ResolveRequest into C's subtree.
then: The Referral lists C's endpoints as [E2, E1], in the new record's order.

title: Keep no record of who asked about whom after answering a resolution

rule.text: answer the request, keep no record of who asked about whom

given: Infra node S has answered a ResolveRequest from authenticated requester Q about subject X, and the session with Q has closed.
when: S's persistent state and logs are inspected.
then: No record pairs Q with X: neither the request nonce, nor the (requester, subject) pair, nor a query-log entry survives the answer.
interpretation: The obligation is a commitment the protocol cannot enforce (design §1.1); the test checks the reference implementation's own storage and treats any retained pairing as a failure.

title: Accept a registration only over the owner's own session

rule.text: The authenticated peer MUST be the owner named in the entry.
Accept registrations only from the owner's own session

given: Owner O has signed a CatalogEntry naming O; O and another client P both hold sessions with host H.
when: O submits the entry over O's session; P submits the same bytes over P's session.
then: O's submission is answered with code 0 and the entry is served; P's is answered with code 1 and the served entry is unchanged.

title: Refuse a registration for a keyhash already served under a different owner

rule.text: A host refuses a registration for a keyhash it already serves under a different owner
Refuse a registration for a keyhash you already serve under a different owner.

given: Host H serves resource keyhash R registered by owner O1.
when: Owner O2 submits a valid entry naming R over O2's session.
then: The reply carries code 1 and H still serves O1's entry for R.

title: Replace on re-registration, retain nothing superseded, archive nothing

rule.text: Re-registering by the same owner replaces the entry, and the old one is gone.
Do not retain superseded registrations
A registration is not archived

given: Owner O has an entry E1 for R served by H.
when: O submits a new entry E2 for R, and the test inspects H's storage and archive.
then: Queries return E2 and never E1, E1 is absent from H's storage, and H's archive did not advance.

title: Default a first registration's discover scope to self

rule.text: with no existing rule, the default is ; `self`, the least-disclosing scope

given: Owner O registers R with H for the first time with field 2 absent.
when: O queries H, and another horizon member M queries H.
then: O's reply carries R's entry; M's does not.

title: Withdraw by re-registering with scope self, and propagate nothing

rule.text: It re-registers the resource with a requested `discover_scope` of self, which no asker but the owner satisfies
Withdrawal is not a propagated message.

given: Owner O's entry for R is visible to horizon member M at host H.
when: O re-registers R requesting scope self, then M queries.
then: M's reply omits R, and no TopologyPush or other frame carrying the entry leaves H.

title: Refuse an asker outside your horizon by closing the stream

rule.text: An asker outside the answering node's horizon is refused before the application reply.
Close the stream; do not return an empty `CatalogReply`.

given: A node X outside H's horizon holds a session with H.
when: X sends a CatalogQuery.
then: The stream is closed and no CatalogReply, empty or otherwise, is sent.

title: Order entries by resource then owner keyhash, return 111, and name the first withheld type

rule.text: orders qualifying entries by resource keyhash, then by owner keyhash, and returns the first 111
the continuation names the type of the first entry it withheld

given: H holds 113 entries visible to asker M.
when: M sends an unfiltered CatalogQuery.
then: The reply's field 2 holds the first 111 entries in ascending resource-then-owner keyhash order and field 3 names the service type of the 112th.

title: Return the owner's signature unchanged and add none

rule.text: Return the owner's signature unchanged, and add none of your own.
An entry is signed once, at registration, and that signature is reused for every answer.

given: Owner O registered entry E with H; the test recorded E's bytes.
when: Two different askers query H.
then: Each reply carries E byte-for-byte, with O's signature and no signature by H.

title: Store an entry whose scope you cannot compute, and grant nothing from it

rule.text: A scope the evaluator cannot compute is structurally valid and ineffective.
A decoder MUST NOT reject it.

given: An entry whose connect_scope names a position H cannot resolve, submitted by its owner over the owner's session.
when: H processes it and a member requests the resource.
then: The registration is answered code 0 and the entry is served; the scope grants nothing, so the request is decided by the role row alone. An implementation that rejects the entry fails.

title: Retain and surface an unknown data_practice value

rule.text: Unknown values are retained and surfaced, not rejected

given: An entry whose field 9 carries a value outside the four defined, correctly signed, and a client with a display hook.
when: The owner registers it and a member's client fetches it.
then: Registration is accepted, the reply carries field 9 unchanged, and the client's hook records that a declaration exists and is unrecognised. An implementation that rejects the entry fails.

title: Never process a resource request from early data, and carry one request per stream

rule.text: a `ResourceRequest` stream is never processed in early data, whatever the method inside
one request per stream
A `ResourceRequest` on a new bidirectional stream

given: Client C resumes a session with H using 0-RTT and holds connect on resource R.
when: C sends a ResourceRequest for R on a new bidirectional stream in early data, and later two requests on one stream.
then: No ResourceResponse and no backend traffic for the early-data request are observed before the handshake completes; on the shared stream only the first request is answered.
interpretation: What happens to a second request on one stream is not stated; the test asserts only that it is not answered as a second exchange.

title: Evaluate a resource request in the normative order and answer with the one code that step yields

rule.text: Evaluation order is normative
Availability is checked last, so a role-holder learns the service is down and a non-role-holder never does.
Evaluate in the order `wire-format.md` §11 gives

given: Host H with resource R owned by O and a stopped package, and six requesters: a stranger; a member lacking a SubtreeAck; a member with an ack and no connect; a member with connect sending malformed HTTP; a member with connect sending a well-formed request; the same with the package running.
when: Each sends a ResourceRequest for R.
then: The six responses carry codes 1, 4, 5, 3, 2 and 0 respectively, and only the last reaches the backend.

title: Answer a non-member with refused for everything, existing keyhash or not

rule.text: A non-member gets `refused` for everything
a keyhash naming nothing returns the same code

given: A stranger S with a session to H, which serves R and nothing named Q.
when: S requests R, then Q.
then: Both responses carry code 1 and nothing else, and no backend traffic follows.

title: Decide a request from the materialised row, and refuse to materialise a row wider than 64 roles

rule.text: Authorisation at request time is a lookup, never a predicate evaluation
refuse to materialise one wider

given: A predicate whose evaluation would now exclude member M, unevaluated since M's row granted connect; and an operator configuring a row of 65 roles.
when: M requests the resource; the operator saves the configuration.
then: M's request is delivered on the strength of the row; the 65-role row is refused at configuration and no request ever yields a code for it.

title: Strip caller rhtn headers, insert your own, and mint one session identifier per resource

rule.text: the node strips inbound `rhtn-*` headers
It is also per resource.
`rhtn-roles` may be empty, and that is not an error.
Mint the session identifier per resource, not per connection.

given: Member M with connect and no application roles on hosted resources R1 and R2, sending requests that carry a forged rhtn-roles header.
when: M requests R1 and R2 over one session.
then: Each backend receives rhtn-principal, rhtn-audience naming itself, rhtn-session and an empty rhtn-roles, with the forged value absent; the two session identifiers differ.

title: Parse and re-serialise, reject the ambiguous, and emit exactly one message

rule.text: Emit exactly one message per `ResourceRequest`.
Reject rather than normalise anything ambiguous
Reject anything asking for an exchange other than one request and one response

given: A member with connect sends, in turn, a request with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, one whose body encodes a second request line, and a CONNECT request.
when: H processes each.
then: Each is answered code 3 and nothing reaches the backend.

title: Never retry a failed handoff on your own

rule.text: the gateway NEVER retries on its own

given: The backend for R accepts a connection and fails mid-request.
when: A member with connect sends a request.
then: Exactly one attempt reaches the backend and the response carries code 2.

title: End the resource-facing session on a role change, and leave the transport session alone

rule.text: the session dropped is the resource-facing one
The transport session is untouched
An in-flight request completes under the state it started with.

given: Member M holds connect on R with a long-running request in flight.
when: The operator revokes M's grant during the request, then M sends another.
then: The in-flight request completes and its response is delivered; the next request is answered code 5; M's QUIC session to H stays open throughout.

title: Expose no network primitive to a hosted package

rule.text: the hooks do not exist
no topology, no liveness state, no queue contents, no prekey requests, no role-evaluation inputs

given: A package whose manifest imports a binding for topology, queue contents, prekeys or role inputs, on a host using the expected component-model sandbox.
when: The host instantiates it.
then: Instantiation fails for want of the import, and the host's export list contains no such binding.
interpretation: The sandbox mechanism is an implementation choice the requirement calls expected rather than mandated; the test assumes a capability-based component host.

title: Acknowledge a subtree automatically under policy, without prompting, and treat it as lapsed when the relationship ends

rule.text: Issue it automatically, under a policy the operator set beforehand.
Do not prompt per adoption.
Treat it as lapsed when the relationship it describes ends

given: Host H with policy set to acknowledge every position, a prompt hook, and subordinate S who adopts a grand-subordinate G.
when: G's adoption reaches H; later S departs.
then: A SubtreeAck for G is issued with no prompt recorded; after S's departure G's request for H's resource is answered code 4.

title: Accept a brokered registration with no local backend

rule.text: A host refusing every entry that lacks a locally installed package refuses valid brokered registrations.

given: Owner O submits an entry whose field 5 names an external endpoint and for which H hosts no package.
when: H processes it.
then: The reply carries code 0. An implementation requiring a local package fails.

title: Store an abuse report only from the resource it names, and carry it nowhere

rule.text: The signing key's ; keyhash MUST equal field 1
An abuse report has no carriage, and needs none.

given: Resource R hosted at owner O's node produces a report signed by R, and a forged one signed by another key naming R.
when: O's node processes both and the test watches its sessions.
then: The first is stored for O; the second is rejected; no report bytes leave the node.

title: Treat a repeated continuation as truncation, not another page

rule.text: A repeated continuation means truncation, not another page.
MUST NOT loop

given: A client sweeping H, which returns a full page with a continuation naming a type the client has already filtered on.
when: The client follows the sweep.
then: The client asks H for that type at most once more, marks H's portion of its view truncated, and stops.

title: Route to a brokered service only when it matches the signed entry

rule.text: Confirm a brokered service matches the signed `CatalogEntry`
Do not present resources the user cannot use.

given: A client holding a signed entry for brokered resource R whose field 5 names endpoint X, and a broker presenting endpoint Y.
when: The user opens R.
then: The client routes no traffic to Y, and shows the owner named in the entry; a resource the catalog page filtered out is not shown.

title: Report primary mode to a client attaching to its own serving node.

rule.text: Determine the attachment mode from local topology. A client not in this node's subtree is in failover, and report it.
Light client dials out to its serving infra node. The nearest infrastructure node on its patron chain, which is not necessarily its patron

given: Infra node N holds an adoption of light client C directly under it, so N is C's nearest infrastructure ancestor. The heartbeat interval is unset (design §21.1) and is a test parameter: the node advertises the harness's chosen value I, in seconds within 1..3600, in AttachAck field 3.
when: C dials N and sends Attach with field 1 equal to its own keyhash.
then: N answers with AttachAck whose field 1 (mode) is 0 and whose field 3 is I.

title: Accept a client whose patron is a light client, on the walk-up to infrastructure.

rule.text: Accept attachment from any node whose nearest infrastructure ancestor is this node, and from siblings' clients in failover
A light client whose patron is itself a light client (§3.3 permits this) walks up until it reaches infrastructure.

given: Infra node N has adopted light client P; P has adopted light client C. C's nearest infrastructure ancestor is therefore N, which is not its patron. The heartbeat interval is unset (design §21.1) and is a test parameter: the node advertises the harness's chosen value I, in seconds within 1..3600, in AttachAck field 3.
when: C dials N and sends Attach.
then: N does not close the connection with application close code 1; it answers with AttachAck whose field 1 (mode) is 0.

title: Send the first heartbeat after one full interval, counter 0, then one per interval.

rule.text: Both sides send one Heartbeat per advertised interval, so liveness is bidirectional and the interval is the serving node's to set.
counter 0 is sent after one interval, not immediately

given: A session between C and N is established (AttachAck received). The heartbeat interval is unset (design §21.1) and is a test parameter: the node advertises the harness's chosen value I, in seconds within 1..3600, in AttachAck field 3. Stream 0 is observed in both directions from the moment AttachAck is sent.
when: Three intervals of I seconds elapse with no other traffic.
then: Each side's first Heartbeat carries counter 0 and is sent no earlier than I seconds after AttachAck; each side's next two carry counters 1 and 2, one per interval.

title: Reset liveness on any valid beat with an unseen counter, so one lost beat does not fail over.

rule.text: valid beat carrying a counter not yet seen resets
Liveness rule: a peer is considered failed after 3 consecutive missed intervals

given: A session between C and N with interval I; the harness sits on the path and can drop individual frames. C holds a sibling list from AttachAck.
when: The harness drops N's Heartbeat with counter 1 and delivers counters 2, 3, 4 and onward on time, for at least six intervals.
then: C stays in the session on N: it opens no connection to any sibling and continues sending its own Heartbeats to N throughout.

title: Count a malformed heartbeat as absence: no immediate close, three misses still govern.

rule.text: A malformed heartbeat counts as absence, not as a fault. It does not reset the detector and does not itself close the session; three missed intervals still govern.

given: A session between C and N with interval I. The harness replaces every Heartbeat from C with a malformed frame carrying the Heartbeat frame type.
when: Three full intervals elapse with only malformed frames arriving from C.
then: N does not close the session on receiving a malformed frame; after three full intervals N's inspectable reachability state for C reads unreachable, not before.

title: Fail over when only payload traffic arrives, since payload does not reset the detector.

rule.text: Unrelated payload or application traffic must not, since it would let incidental activity conceal failure of the very path the detector tests. Present encoding: only a Heartbeat resets the counter.
after 3 consecutive missed intervals, the client attaches to another party in the same replication set as its serving node

given: C is in a session on N with interval I and holds sibling S's SiblingRef with KeyMaterial from AttachAck. N is scripted to keep sending payload frames on unidirectional streams while sending no Heartbeat.
when: Three full intervals elapse in which N sends payload but no Heartbeat.
then: C dials S and receives an AttachAck from S with field 1 (mode) equal to 1.

title: Count intervals that elapsed during a suspension on waking, not timer callbacks.

rule.text: Misses are counted by elapsed full intervals on a local monotonic clock, not by delivered timer callbacks.
A mobile runtime suspended for three intervals has missed three on waking

given: C is in a session on N with interval I and holds sibling S's SiblingRef with KeyMaterial. N is stopped.
when: C's process is suspended for longer than three intervals and then resumed.
then: On resuming, C dials S before another full interval elapses, and receives an AttachAck from S with field 1 equal to 1.
interpretation: 'Has missed three on waking' is read as failover beginning on waking; the one-interval bound is the test's, since wire-format.md §8.2 leaves timeout and backoff to local policy.

title: Attach to a sibling of the serving node after three missed intervals, and be told the session is degraded.

rule.text: after 3 consecutive missed intervals, the client attaches to another party in the same replication set as its serving node, and the resulting session is degraded.
The serving node determines the mode; the client is told.

given: Infra nodes N and S are siblings (design §3.4); C is adopted under N and attached to N with interval I; N's AttachAck listed S with KeyMaterial.
when: N stops sending Heartbeats and all other frames for three full intervals.
then: C dials S; S answers with AttachAck whose field 1 (mode) is 1.

title: Accept a sibling's client that fails over from its persisted list when its serving node is unreachable at attach time.

rule.text: a client whose serving node is unreachable at attach time uses its cached sibling list immediately.
Persist the cached sibling list across restarts.
Accept attachment from any node whose nearest infrastructure ancestor is this node, and from siblings' clients in failover

given: C previously attached to N and received an AttachAck listing sibling S with KeyMaterial; C's process has since exited. N is unreachable (no route) at the time of the next attach.
when: C starts and performs a fresh attach.
then: C dials S without first waiting three heartbeat intervals, and S accepts: it does not close with application close code 1 and returns AttachAck with field 1 equal to 1.

title: Produce no countersignature in a degraded session.

rule.text: That party holds the replicated state but not the authority to countersign.
Payload flows; the subnet-scoped transactions the patron countersigns wait for the patron

given: N is both patron and serving node of C; N is dark and C holds a degraded session on N's sibling S (AttachAck field 1 equal to 1).
when: C submits a subnet-scoped transaction that requires its patron's countersignature on the degraded session, and also sends ordinary payload.
then: No transaction countersigned by S comes into existence, at S or at C; the payload is carried.
interpretation: How a countersignature request travels on a session and how its non-performance is signalled are not encoded; the test observes only the absence of a countersignature by S.

title: Stay on the sibling while the degraded session lasts, even after the serving node returns.

rule.text: A client on a sibling stays there until that session ends; the next fresh attach tries its actual serving node first.
No automatic failback: the client stays on the sibling until that session ends, and the next fresh attach tries its actual serving node first.

given: C holds a degraded session on S with interval I after N went dark.
when: N becomes reachable again and stays reachable for at least six intervals while the degraded session continues.
then: C opens no connection to N during that time and keeps exchanging Heartbeats with S.

title: Try the actual serving node first on the next fresh attach after a degraded session.

rule.text: A client on a sibling stays there until that session ends; the next fresh attach tries its actual serving node first.
the next fresh attach tries its actual serving node first

given: C holds a degraded session on S; N has since become reachable again.
when: C's session on S ends (C closes it) and C performs a fresh attach.
then: C's first dial is to N, and N answers with AttachAck whose field 1 (mode) is 0.

title: Mark a client unreachable when its heartbeats stop.

rule.text: the serving node marks the client unreachable; material for it queues as it always did, and delivery waits for its return.
Liveness rule: a peer is considered failed after 3 consecutive missed intervals
Store the resulting reachability state, not the update history

given: C is attached to N with interval I; N exposes its reachability state per client to the test.
when: The harness blackholes all packets from C to N for three full intervals.
then: N's reachability state for C reads unreachable after the third full interval, and read reachable at every inspection before it.

title: Replicate a client's unreachable state to the serving node's siblings.

rule.text: This state replicates to siblings, or a sibling answering during failover has no idea of the client's status.
Siblings replicate each other's topology and trust-bearing transaction history (up to f−1 = 9).

given: N and S are siblings; C is attached to N with interval I; both nodes expose their reachability state per client to the test. Replication between N and S is running.
when: The harness blackholes all packets from C to N for three full intervals, and replication is allowed to proceed.
then: S's reachability state for C reads unreachable.
interpretation: No wire object carrying the replicated reachability state is specified; the test observes S's state and does not check what carried it or how soon it arrived.

title: Bind a 0-RTT reattach only after the handshake completes, and still complete it.

rule.text: A server MUST NOT process an Attach received in TLS 1.3 0-RTT early data — reject it or defer it until handshake completion.
0-RTT resumption makes frequent reattachment cheap, which permits a lazy heartbeat and saves battery.

given: C completed an earlier session with N and holds a TLS 1.3 resumption ticket from it. The harness observes the connection and knows when its handshake completes.
when: C reconnects with 0-RTT and sends Attach in early data.
then: No AttachAck is sent before the handshake of that connection completes; after completion an AttachAck arrives, either for the deferred early Attach or for an Attach C sends after the handshake if the early one was rejected.

title: Add a subordinate and its sibling relationships to the table on a verified adoption

rule.text: Patron accepts a new subordinate. Also implicitly authorises sibling peering among that patron's children.
Authorised implicitly by the patron's adoption transaction, with no separate agreement.

given: Observer O's table, fed verified transactions directly since propagation is out of scope, holding patron P with one subordinate C; a proof-of-presence record between P and N.
when: O verifies an adoption of N under P whose field 8 names that record.
then: O's table answers: N's patrons include P; P's subordinates are {C, N}; C's siblings include N and N's siblings include C.

title: Hold a second adoption beside the first: adopting elsewhere leaves the old binding in view

rule.text: Without it, a node that adopts elsewhere remains in the old subtree's view indefinitely, since adoption says nothing about existing bindings.
the protocol has no concept of a node's set of patrons

given: O's table holding N adopted under P1, series s1. An adoption of N under P2 carrying either P1's countersignature as former patron or a proof of presence between N and P2, opening series s2.
when: O verifies the second adoption, with no departure from P1 signed.
then: O's table answers N's patrons = {P1, P2}; N remains among P1's subordinates; the second adoption is accepted rather than rejected as a duplicate binding, and it does not replace the first.

title: End only the named relationship on a departure

rule.text: Single signature: the departing node.
Moving between patrons remains adopt at the destination, depart the origin, in either order, with no requirement to do both

given: O's table holding N under P1 and under P2, as TOP-02 leaves it.
when: O verifies a departure signed by N alone with field 2 = P1.
then: O's table answers N's patrons = {P2}; N is no longer among P1's subordinates and no longer a sibling of P1's other children; N's binding under P2 is unchanged.

title: Leave a departed node in the table as a root when it has no other binding

rule.text: Required for a node to become a root by its own action.
Roots have none, which is an ordinary state rather than an error

given: O's table holding N under P and under nobody else.
when: O verifies N's departure from P.
then: O's table answers N's patrons = {} and still lists N as a node; N is removed from P's subordinates; no error is raised for a patronless node.

title: End one relationship and nothing else on a disavowal

rule.text: Disavowal is positional: it ends one patron-subordinate relationship and nothing else. The node remains in the tree and may be adopted elsewhere within the same subnet

given: O's table holding N under P and under Q, and M under N.
when: O verifies a disavowal signed by P alone with field 2 = N and reason code 0.
then: O's table answers N's patrons = {Q}; N is removed from P's subordinates; M's patrons still include N; N remains a node in the table.

title: Apply a disavowal on verification regardless of its timestamp

rule.text: There is no notice period. A disavowal takes effect when signed
A disavowal takes effect when it is signed.

given: O's table holding N under P; O's clock reads t_now.
when: O verifies a disavowal of N by P whose timestamp is t_now plus seven days and not earlier than the effective time of P's predecessor record.
then: O's table removes N from P's subordinates on verification; the relationship is not held open until the timestamp, and the record is not rejected for its timestamp.

title: Issue a subtree acknowledgement under standing policy without operator interaction

rule.text: Issued by the grandpatron's node, not by its operator.
Issue it automatically, under a policy the operator set beforehand.

given: Infra node G with subordinate P and an acknowledgement policy, set beforehand, that acknowledges every adoption under P; no operator session is open.
when: G's node verifies an adoption of N under P with txid a.
then: G's node emits a SubtreeAck with field 1 = a, field 2 = G, field 3 = N, and field 5 a signature by G that verifies over fields 1 to 4 with external_aad rhtn/1:subtree-ack; no prompt and no operator input occurs between verification and emission.

title: Enter an adoption in the table whether or not the grandpatron acknowledges it

rule.text: It does not gate the adoption. The adoption is complete and valid with the node and patron signatures (wire-format.md §4.1); it is signed and propagated whether or not the grandpatron acknowledges it.

given: Tables at P and at P's sibling S holding P under G; G's node is offline, or its policy acknowledges nobody.
when: P and N sign an adoption of N under P and S verifies it, with no SubtreeAck ever arriving.
then: S's table answers N's patrons = {P} and lists N under P; S holds no acknowledgement for N; the adoption is neither held pending nor rejected for the missing acknowledgement.

title: Discard a subtree acknowledgement when the relationship it describes ends

rule.text: It lapses when the acknowledged relationship ends. If the grandpatron disavows the patron, or the patron departs, the acknowledgement describes a subtree the node is no longer in and confers nothing.
Discard it when it lapses

given: A holder H, G's sibling, whose table holds P under G and N under P, and who holds G's SubtreeAck for N.
when: H verifies P's departure from G; in a second run, G's disavowal of P.
then: In both runs H's list of held acknowledgements no longer contains the acknowledgement for N, no revocation object having been received; N's binding under P is still in H's table.

title: Create no binding from a subtree acknowledgement whose adoption is not held

rule.text: It attests membership of a subtree, not identity. The adoption's own signatures carry identity.
It says nothing about identity. The adoption's signatures carry that. Do not let a SubtreeAck stand in for evidence about who someone is.

given: A holder H whose table holds P under G and no adoption of N, and who holds G's key material.
when: H receives a well-formed SubtreeAck signed by G naming an adoption txid a and node N, with a not held by H.
then: H's table answers N's patrons = {} and does not list N under P; the acknowledgement's signature verifies, and no table entry for N results from it.
interpretation: The sections quoted say an acknowledgement carries no identity evidence; the test reads that as an acknowledgement alone never creating a binding, which no sentence states directly.

title: Form a subnet from two Genesis identities: a formation record, then one adopts the other as first root

rule.text: One adopts the other and becomes the subnet's first root.
They perform a proof-of-presence ceremony with no witnesses and no verifiers.

given: Two fresh keys A and B with empty archives and empty tables; A runs an infra instance, its static address outside the test's scope.
when: A and B sign a formation presence record, subtype 1 with no witnesses, no verifier responses and genesis back-pointers, then an adoption of B under A whose field 8 names that record; both tables verify both.
then: Both tables answer: A's patrons = {}, A's subordinates = {B}, B's patrons = {A}. Each archive holds the formation record as its first transaction and the adoption as its second, the adoption's back-pointer for each signer naming the formation record.

title: Do not apply an adoption whose named presence record is not between these two parties

rule.text: The check is that the record exists and names these two parties, both of which are body fields.
That is an evaluation step, not a structural one

given: O's table holding P; a presence record between P and a third party Z held by O; a structurally valid adoption of N under P whose field 8 names that record.
when: O verifies the adoption structurally, then evaluates it, dereferencing field 8, before applying it to the table.
then: Structural verification reports valid. Evaluation reports the presence reference unsatisfied, the record naming P and Z rather than P and N, and O's table does not gain N under P.
interpretation: Whether a failed evaluation keeps the adoption out of the table is not stated; wire-format.md §3.4 makes taking effect a separate question from validity, and the test reads the evaluation step as the gate on applying the binding.

title: Serve a light client whose patron is a light client: it attaches to the nearest infrastructure ancestor as primary

rule.text: Every light client beneath you attaches to you — not only your direct subordinates, since design §14.1.2 has a client walk up past light-client patrons to the nearest infrastructure.
Accept attachment from any node whose nearest infrastructure ancestor is this node

given: Infra node I whose table holds light client A under I and light client B under A; B's client holds the same topology.
when: B dials its serving node and attaches.
then: B's dial goes to I, not to A; I accepts and its AttachAck field 1 is 0, primary; I's table lists B among its attached light clients by path, beneath A.

title: Refuse a proposed patron only when the table places it in the node's own down-line

rule.text: Rejection is on positive knowledge only: reject where local topology establishes that the proposed patron is at or below the node, and never for absence of knowledge.

given: Node N's table holding M under N and M2 under M, and holding nothing about a node X.
when: N's client is asked to adopt under M2, and separately to adopt under X, ceremony evidence being supplied in both cases.
then: The proposal to adopt under M2 is refused by the local check, which reports that M2 lies below N, and no adoption is signed. The proposal to adopt under X is not refused by the check, and an adoption of N under X is signed.

title: Replace the old key with the successor on a recovery adoption inside the horizon

rule.text: members holding the old key remove it from their records and overwrite it with the new one

given: O's table holding identity K_old under P. A recovery adoption of K_new under P carrying a Recovery block with prior_key = K_old, structurally valid and passing the evidence gate; the evidence is supplied by fixture, its generation being out of scope.
when: O verifies and applies the recovery adoption.
then: O's table answers K_new's patrons = {P}; K_old is no longer listed under P and is not a current key in O's table; O holds exactly one current key for the identity.

title: Hold one current key per identity when two recovery adoptions compete for the same prior key

rule.text: a member receiving two competing recovery adoptions for the same prior_key does not hold both as current — it resolves to one, by which patron it trusts

given: O's table holding K_old under P; two recovery adoptions, K_a under P_a and K_b under P_b, each with prior_key = K_old and each passing the evidence gate; which of P_a and P_b O trusts more is O's own policy, fixed by no document, and the test sets it as a parameter.
when: O verifies and applies both adoptions, in each of the two orders.
then: O's table holds exactly one current key for the identity, K_a when O prefers P_a and K_b otherwise, the same one in both orders; both K_a and K_b are present as nodes under their own patrons.
interpretation: Independence from arrival order follows from resolving by patron trust rather than by arrival; no sentence states it.

title: Order a disavowal within the patron's own slot by the patron's timestamp

rule.text: A disavowal is ordered by the patron's own clock.
Field 3 orders the disavowal within the patron's own slot

given: Patron P's table holds N in slot k from an adoption stamped t1; P signs a disavowal of N stamped t2 > t1, then re-adopts N with an adoption stamped t3 > t2 that opens a fresh series.
when: P's records are read after the three, in any arrival order.
then: P's slot k shows N present from t1, empty from t2, and N present again from t3 under the new series; the relationship's status at any time is decided from P's own timestamps and nothing another party signed.

title: Offer only X25519MLKEM768 as the key-exchange group.

rule.text: QUIC with TLS 1.3, key exchange group X25519MLKEM768.
offering only X25519MLKEM768 is what leaves nothing weaker to fall back to.

given: The implementation acts as the dialling party toward a test endpoint that records the TLS ClientHello carried in the QUIC Initial packets (readable with the Initial keys).
when: The implementation opens a connection to that endpoint.
then: The ClientHello's supported_groups extension lists exactly one group, X25519MLKEM768, and its key_share extension carries no share for any other group.

title: Complete no handshake with a peer that offers only weaker groups.

rule.text: That nothing can be negotiated below the named group is this profile's doing, not TLS's
offering only X25519MLKEM768 is what leaves nothing weaker to fall back to.
