given: The implementation acts as the serving node. A test client presents a valid raw public key and ALPN rhtn/1, but its ClientHello supported_groups extension lists only classical groups (X25519 and secp256r1) and no X25519MLKEM768.
when: The test client attempts the handshake.
then: No handshake completes: the connection ends during the handshake, no session is established, and no AttachAck can be obtained on it.

title: Abort the dial when the presented raw public key is not the pinned classical member.

rule.text: The dialling party checks that key is the classical member of the KeyMaterial it has pinned for the keyhash it intended to reach.
a wrong address produces a failed handshake rather than a false identity.
KeyMaterial = [ COSE_Key, COSE_Key ]   ; [classical, post-quantum]

given: The implementation, as dialling party, holds a validated pin for keyhash K: a KeyMaterial that hashes to K. A test endpoint advertised for K completes the TLS handshake with an RFC 7250 raw public key whose SubjectPublicKeyInfo is a valid Ed25519 key that is not the first entry of that KeyMaterial.
when: The implementation dials the endpoint intending to reach K.
then: The handshake does not complete from the implementation's side: the connection is abandoned before any control frame is sent, no Attach frame appears on stream 0, and the dial is reported as a failed handshake rather than as a session with K.

title: Reject an Attach whose field 1 is not the transport-authenticated identity.

rule.text: Authentication is mutual. The serving node authenticates the client the same way, and MUST bind the identity for which session state and queued data are requested to the identity the transport authenticated, rejecting any mismatch.
Present encoding: Attach field 1 must equal the connection-authenticated identity.
There is no AttachNack, and refusal is carried as a QUIC close code.

given: The implementation acts as serving node S and holds queued items for keyhash B, inspectable by the test. A test client holding keypair A completes a mutual raw-public-key handshake presenting A's classical component, so the connection-authenticated identity is A.
when: The test client sends a well-formed Attach whose field 1 is B, with a Capabilities map in field 3.
then: No AttachAck is issued on the connection, nothing queued for B is delivered on it, and S's queue for B is unchanged. No AttachNack or other refusal frame appears on stream 0.

title: Negotiate the application protocol rhtn/1.

rule.text: ALPN: rhtn/1

given: The implementation is exercised in both roles: as dialling party toward a test serving node that records the ClientHello, and as serving node receiving a ClientHello whose ALPN list contains rhtn/1.
when: A handshake is run in each role.
then: As dialling party, the ClientHello's ALPN extension carries rhtn/1. As serving node, the negotiated application protocol is rhtn/1 and the handshake completes.

title: Frame every stream-0 control message as a big-endian length over a typed CBOR array.

rule.text: Stream 0 carries length-delimited, type-tagged frames.
frame = u32-be length || deterministic CBOR of [ uint frame_type, body ]
the control frames of §8.0 — session control (attach, heartbeat, sibling updates) and topology propagation (push, memo)

given: The implementation attaches as client with the identity, attestation and named capabilities of the corpus's Attach fixture, and answers as serving node with the inputs of the corpus's AttachAck fixture; the heartbeat interval in the ack is a test-chosen value in 1..=3600 seconds, since design §21.1 leaves it unset.
when: The client attaches.
then: The first bytes the client sends on stream 0 are a 4-byte big-endian length N followed by exactly N bytes of deterministic CBOR decoding to a two-element array [1, Attach], whose body with any greased capability entry removed equals the corpus fixture body. The serving node's reply on stream 0 is likewise a length prefix followed by CBOR decoding to [2, AttachAck]. Neither frame appears on any other stream.

title: Skip an unknown control frame sized at the bound, even before the AttachAck.

rule.text: Unknown frame types MUST be skipped, not rejected.
length counts the CBOR bytes that follow it, and is bounded at 64 KB — exactly 65,536 bytes
Unknown control frames may precede AttachAck and are skipped as always

given: The implementation, as client, has completed the handshake and sent Attach to a test serving node. Separately, the implementation as serving node has an attached session with a test client. The AttachAck's heartbeat interval is a test-chosen value in 1..=3600 seconds (design §21.1 leaves it unset).
when: The test serving node sends on stream 0 a frame whose type is 99 and whose CBOR payload [99, bstr] is exactly 65,536 bytes, so the length prefix reads 65,536, followed by a valid AttachAck. In the other role, the test client sends the same 65,536-byte unknown frame mid-session.
then: In neither role is the connection closed. As client, the AttachAck that follows is accepted and the session is attached in the mode the ack states. As serving node, a request opened on a bidirectional stream after the unknown frame is answered.

title: End the session on a declared control-frame length above 65,536.

rule.text: A declared length above the bound is a protocol error, and it ends the session

given: An attached session between the implementation and a test peer, exercised with the implementation in each role.
when: The test peer sends on stream 0 a 4-byte length prefix reading 65,537, followed by bytes.
then: The implementation closes the connection: a CONNECTION_CLOSE is observed, and no frame sent on that session after the oversized prefix is acted on. The close code is not stated by the profile and is not checked.

title: Discard a malformed control frame of a known type whole and keep the session.

rule.text: A malformed control frame of a known type is discarded whole, and the session survives
a malformed SiblingUpdate is ignored whole with the previous list standing
replaces the client's cached list ENTIRELY.

given: The implementation, as client, is attached to a test serving node and holds cached sibling list L from the AttachAck; the ack's heartbeat interval is a test-chosen value in 1..=3600 seconds (design §21.1 leaves it unset).
when: The test serving node sends on stream 0 a frame [4, body] within the length bound whose body is not a well-formed SiblingUpdate (a text string), then a valid SiblingUpdate carrying list L2.
then: After the malformed frame the connection remains open and the cached sibling list is still L. After the valid update the cached sibling list is L2.

title: Tolerate a capability parameter whose id is not recognised.

rule.text: Every implementation MUST tolerate receiving parameters whose ids it does not recognise. That is checkable by anyone: send one and observe whether the session continues.
Unknown parameters MUST be ignored, never rejected.
Tolerating unknown parameters is mandatory and checkable; sending greased ones is self-interested rather than obligatory.

given: A test peer builds a Capabilities map holding one entry whose id is a random 64-bit value derived from no name the implementation knows, with an 8-byte value. As serving node the implementation receives it in Attach field 3; as client it receives it in AttachAck field 5, with a test-chosen heartbeat interval in 1..=3600 seconds (design §21.1 leaves it unset).
when: The frame carrying the unrecognised parameter arrives.
then: The session continues in both roles: the serving node answers with an AttachAck, the client attaches on the ack it receives, and no close and no error frame follows the unrecognised parameter.

title: Attach when the peer advertises no capabilities and greases nothing.

rule.text: Absence of a capability is never a connection failure. Parameters set limits; they do not gate the session.
Sending is not a MUST, because nothing could check it.
A required map with no entries is encoded as an empty map — Capabilities in Attach and AttachAck is the case in point, since a peer advertising nothing must still send the field.

given: A test peer sends a Capabilities map with no entries, the empty map: it advertises none of the capabilities the implementation itself supports and carries no greased parameter. As serving node the implementation receives it in Attach; as client, in an AttachAck whose heartbeat interval is a test-chosen value in 1..=3600 seconds (design §21.1 leaves it unset).
when: The frame carrying the empty Capabilities map arrives.
then: The session is established in both roles: the serving node sends an AttachAck, the client attaches on the ack, and the connection is not closed. No absent capability and no absent greased parameter is reported as an error.

title: Send a greased capability parameter in every session.

rule.text: The reference implementation sends one greased parameter per session: a random 64-bit id and a value of 8 random bytes.

given: The reference implementation, in both roles, with the list of capability names it publishes and the ids derived from them.
when: Two sessions are opened, and the Attach it sends as client and the AttachAck it sends as serving node are captured in each.
then: Each captured Capabilities map contains an entry whose id is the id of no published name and whose value is 8 bytes long, and the id of that entry differs between the two sessions.

title: Refuse an attach with application close code 1 and no frame in reply.

rule.text: There is no AttachNack, and refusal is carried as a QUIC close code.
A node refusing an attach by policy closes the connection with application close code 1 (refused) in CONNECTION_CLOSE.
Code 0 is not used for refusal, since it is the conventional no-error close.

given: The implementation acts as serving node S with a local attach policy that refuses client C; the policy itself is local and unspecified by the design, so the test supplies one. C completes a mutual raw-public-key handshake.
when: C sends a well-formed Attach whose field 1 is C.
then: S closes the connection with a CONNECTION_CLOSE carrying application close code 1, not 0, and sends no frame of any type on stream 0 in reply: no AttachAck and no refusal frame.

title: Treat close code 1 as the node's answer, not the endpoint's.

rule.text: A client seeing it MUST treat the refusal as that node's answer, not that endpoint's — its other addresses will say the same
a primary's refusal does not open sibling failover
treat a policy refusal as that node's answer rather than that endpoint's — trying its other addresses will not change it.

given: The implementation, as client C, knows its serving node S by two NetworkPoints and holds a cached sibling list from an earlier session. Retry timing and backoff are local policy and are parameterised by the test.
when: C dials S's first endpoint, completes the handshake, sends Attach, and receives a CONNECTION_CLOSE with application close code 1.
then: Within the test's observation window C makes no connection attempt to S's second endpoint and dials no cached sibling; the attach attempt ends as refused.

title: Keep the session across a client address change without a new attach.

rule.text: Connection migration relied upon for mobile IP change
Mobile clients change IP constantly, and QUIC's connection migration survives that natively where ordinary single-path TCP does not

given: An attached session between the implementation as client C and the implementation as serving node S, with a test-chosen heartbeat interval in 1..=3600 seconds (design §21.1 leaves it unset). The test can enqueue an item at S for C.
when: C's UDP source address and port change mid-session (a new local socket, or a simulated NAT rebinding) and C continues the same QUIC connection from the new address; the test then enqueues an item for C.
then: No new Attach or AttachAck is exchanged, heartbeats continue in both directions on the same connection from the new address, and the item enqueued after the change is delivered to C over that same connection.
interpretation: The serving node is taken to permit client-initiated migration, which RFC 9000 lets a server disable; the documents state that migration is relied upon and place no obligation on the operator in infra-client-requirements.md §7.

title: Process an Attach carried in 0-RTT early data only after that connection's handshake completes.

rule.text: A server MUST NOT process an Attach received in TLS 1.3 0-RTT early data — reject it or defer it until handshake completion.
Early data is replayable, and a replayed Attach re-binds session state
§8.2's rule for Attach is this rule's other instance, on the other stream class.

given: Client C holds a resumption ticket from a completed session with the implementation as serving node S, and S holds a queued item for C. The AttachAck's heartbeat interval is a test-chosen value in 1..=3600 seconds (design §21.1 leaves it unset).
when: C opens connection A and sends Attach with field 1 = C as 0-RTT early data. The test captures A's early-data packets and replays them as a second connection B whose handshake it never completes. A's handshake then completes.
then: On A, no AttachAck and no queued delivery is observed before A's handshake completes; afterwards either an AttachAck follows or none is ever sent for that Attach. On B, no AttachAck is ever sent and the queued item is not delivered: it remains queued at S or is delivered on A alone.
interpretation: Handshake completion is read as completion of the handshake of the connection that carried the early data, as the compliant Tamarin theory states it; the wire says only 'until handshake completion', and a completed handshake on A is taken not to admit B's replay.

title: Reject a COSE container that departs from the profile: a carried payload, a filled outer header, an entry set that is not one hybrid pair

rule.text: All signatures in this profile are DETACHED.
the outer COSE_Sign.protected is empty
A group with fewer than two entries, two entries of the same alg, or any alg outside the profile is malformed.

given: A valid adoption envelope; the same with its COSE payload slot carrying h'00', with its outer protected header nonempty, and with its outer unprotected header nonempty. A valid transfer adoption whose former-patron block is replaced by an empty COSE_Sign, by one carrying a single entry, by one carrying the classical entry twice, by one with the post-quantum entry first, and by one whose payload slot carries h'00', the body re-signed by the node and patron each time. A valid endpoint record whose COSE_Sign1 payload slot carries h'00'.
when: Each is decoded and verified.
then: The valid objects are accepted. Every variant is rejected: the envelope variants at the structural layer, the block variants before any signature in the block is checked, and the endpoint record at verification. An implementation that reconstructs the signing input from its own empty headers and nil payload while ignoring what was received fails, as does one that treats an empty block as covered.

title: Require exactly one evidence form on an adoption, and bind a Recovery block's responses to the parties it names

rule.text: EXACTLY ONE of fields 6, 8 and 9 is present
Every response's subject MUST equal the newly adopted node
Every response's field 8 MUST equal prior_key
Every response's verifier MUST differ from its subject

given: A valid adoption on a presence record; the same with field 8 removed, and with a transfer statement added beside it. A valid recovery adoption of a new key under a patron with one genuine match; the same with a response naming a third party as subject, with a response naming another prior key in field 8, with the new key as its own verifier, with no match among the responses, with a selection basis other than met, with one verifier twice, with no response at all, and with the prior key equal to the new key. Every signature is genuine in every variant.
when: Each is parsed as a record.
then: The two valid adoptions parse, and the recovery control verifies. Each variant is rejected at the structural layer, before any signature is checked, naming the rule it broke. An implementation that verifies each embedded signature without checking whom it is about fails.

title: Check a presence record's subtype rules: a formation is genesis-rooted and carries no evidence arrays, a normal record is witnessed, and the participants differ

rule.text: A key may appear in at most one formation record: its first.
a validator checks the subtype, the absent evidence arrays, and the genesis back-pointers
The two participant identities MUST differ.
PRESENT on a normal record (1..=16)

given: A formation between two fresh keys on genesis back-pointers; the same with arbitrary hashes in key 0; a formation for a key that already has a transaction; a witnessed normal record with its subtype flipped to formation; a formation with its subtype flipped to normal; and a formation naming one identity as both participants.
when: Each is parsed as a record, or checked as a body.
then: The genesis-rooted formation parses. Each variant is rejected: the arbitrary and the established key's back-pointers as not the genesis value, the flipped normal record as a formation carrying witnesses, the flipped formation as a normal record without witnesses, and the equal participants as one identity. An implementation that checks the subtype's range and nothing the subtype conditions fails.

title: Check a body against the type its envelope names, with two distinct parties in every two-party type, a peering's evidence present, and a reissue's new series at counter 0

rule.text: the rule holds for every two-party type
without it is MALFORMED
the new series. Its counter is 0

given: A valid departure body enveloped as type 2 and then as type 1; a departure, a disavowal, a reissue and an adoption each naming one identity in both fields 1 and 2; a valid reissue and the same with its new series opening at counter 1; a valid peering and the same without field 8.
when: Each is parsed as a record, or checked as a body.
then: The departure parses as type 2 and is rejected as type 1 for want of a locator: the type comes from the envelope, never from the body's shape. Each one-identity body is rejected, as are the reissue at counter 1 and the peering without its presence record. An implementation that classifies a body by its fields and applies whichever rules the shape suggests fails.

title: Reject a packed path whose byte length, nibble values or pad nibble depart from the encoding, at every decoding boundary

rule.text: The packed byte string MUST be exactly ceil(nibble_count / 2) bytes.
Nibble values MUST be 0-9
On an odd nibble count the unused low nibble of the final byte MUST be zero.

given: Locators whose paths are the empty self-anchor, one nibble with a zero pad, two nibbles, and three nibbles with a zero pad; and locators claiming one nibble over no bytes, carrying a surplus byte, a byte short, a nibble of value 10 in either position, and a nonzero pad nibble on one and on three nibbles. A ResolveRequest whose path claims one nibble over no bytes.
when: Each locator is decoded; the request is decoded, and the same path is asked for its hop indices by another route.
then: The four well-formed paths are accepted. Each departure is rejected, naming the byte length, the nibble value or the pad nibble. The request is refused at decoding, and the hop-index operation on the malformed path returns without indexing past its bytes. An implementation that checks the nibble ceiling alone and then indexes by the claimed count fails.

title: End the binding a departure's series names, in whatever order the departure and its adoption arrive

rule.text: counter incremented within the current series
reconciliation is a replay of the same frames
Remove a child on departure or disavowal.

given: O's table; an adoption of N under P opening series 1, N's departure from P at series 1 counter 1, and a later re-adoption of N under P opening series 2.
when: O applies the departure before its adoption; and applies the three records in each of their six arrival orders.
then: After the departure and then the adoption, N is not among P's subordinates: the departure is held and settled against the adoption its series names. In every order the series-1 binding is ended and the series-2 binding stands open, so N's patrons are {P} by the re-adoption alone. A departure applied twice ends nothing the second time. An implementation that discards a departure arriving before its adoption, or ends whichever open binding it finds first, fails.

title: Keep every accepted message across a restart in its arrival second

rule.text: Undelivered messages queue indefinitely at the recipient's serving node
Queue indefinitely, bounded by a per-subordinate storage cap

given: N's mailbox on disk holding two messages for C that arrived in one second; N restarts within that second and accepts a third for C.
when: C's queue is listed.
then: All three ciphertexts are held, oldest first, and three files exist: the restarted store resumes its sequence past what the directory holds and never creates a file over an existing one. An implementation that restarts its sequence at zero and overwrites fails.

title: End the old credential's service when the node itself applies the recovery, and know it again after a restart

rule.text: Stop serving a binding you have verified superseded
a party holding that knowledge serves nothing under the old key

given: N, a root serving its light client C, with C attached. A recovery adoption of C' claiming C's history under N, which N originates as the countersigning patron. Later, a node started from N's saved topology store.
when: N stores the recovery; C attaches again and a sender submits a message for C; the restarted node is asked about C.
then: N's serving state reports C superseded with no separate call: C's session ends, the fresh attach is refused with close code 1, and the submission is refused as superseded. The restarted node reports C superseded before its first session and refuses C's attach. An implementation whose table learns the recovery while its serving state keeps delivering under the old key fails.

title: Publish own endpoints from what is held: replay an unchanged list, advance the counter for a changed one, one record per relationship line

rule.text: Publishing a changed endpoint list advances the counter
Republishing an unchanged list replays the record already held
publish one record per relationship line
incremented on every position change and on every endpoint change

given: An infra node C adopted at series 1 counter 0, with no endpoint record of its own; then holding one at counter 1 for address A; then bound under a second patron on series 7. A node restarted from its saved store on a new address.
when: C publishes for A, for A again, for B, and for its second line; the restarted node starts.
then: The first record is at counter 1 and the position advances to 1; the second publication for A returns the held bytes and spends nothing; B takes counter 2, the position advances to 2, and the store takes the record as newer; the second line's record is at series 7 counter 1 with the primary line untouched. The restarted node's store holds its record at counter 2 for the new address, the position reads 2, and an unchanged republication replays those bytes. An implementation that publishes counter 1 at every start fails: on a restored store it collides with itself or publishes stale.

title: Read a clock that moves: issuance stamps the current time, and the ladder's intervals elapse on the clock alone

rule.text: Issue fresh, never extend stale.
Outage duration

given: A grandpatron's view whose clock is a source the test moves and never writes through the view; the same for a running patron node, whose view was built at another time.
when: Currency is issued twice with the clock advanced between them; the patron and its sibling are marked dark and the clock, not the view, advances by the grandpatron interval; a client asks the running node for currency at three clock readings.
then: Each attestation's issued_at is the clock's reading at issuance, and expires_at the lifetime past it; the outage stamp is the clock's reading; the grandpatron rung opens once the interval has elapsed on the clock; the running node's view reads the configured clock from start and each answer is issued at the reading current when asked. An implementation that stamps a value set at construction, or that a running node never advances, fails.
interpretation: The design fixes no clock source; the reference node reads one source for every time-dependent decision, its configuration's, and a test substitutes a controllable one.

title: Retain no session history in a running node: recording is a test facility, off unless a configuration turns it on

rule.text: Process liveness updates and discard them.
Do not log queue events

given: A node and a client on their default configurations; a session between them that attaches, exchanges a heartbeat and carries one delivery. A second node whose test configuration turns recording on.
when: The session has run for a heartbeat interval; each side's event log is read; a client attaches to the second node.
then: The first node reports the session live and the client reachable, and both sides' logs are empty: the reachability state is kept and nothing of what passed. The second node's log and its client's each record the attach. An implementation whose sessions append every frame sent and every delivery to a store no configuration turns off fails.

title: Delete a message on delivery and not before: a delivery the peer never took leaves it in the mailbox for the next session

rule.text: Undelivered messages queue indefinitely at the recipient's serving node
Delete on delivery, immediately, leaving nothing recoverable.

given: N holding forty messages for C. C attaches, receives what arrives within a moment, and its connection dies mid-drain; C attaches again later. Separately, C attached and three messages submitted for it.
when: N drains on each attach; the submissions for the attached client are delivered.
then: After the failed session the store still holds every message C never took and none it took; the second AttachAck reports that count and the drain delivers exactly those, so across both sessions every accepted message was received and nothing was lost. For the attached client each message is stored on acceptance and gone once taken. An implementation that empties the mailbox before delivering, or reports success before the peer has taken the message, fails.
interpretation: Taken means the peer acknowledged every byte of the delivery stream, the transport's own boundary; a message whose acknowledgement the failure swallowed may be delivered again, which is the failure mode the design's no-loss rule chooses.

title: Send the currency fallback and a conflict's re-resolution on bidirectional request streams, up sessions the node holds as a client, and take the replies

rule.text: Bidirectional request type 8
Every bidirectional stream opens with a request-type tag.

given: N with a session to X's patron P; and a running N attached upstream to P, where X is P's subordinate. Separately, a fabric on which P is a session N serves.
when: N asks about X's currency; P's attestation comes back; a reply naming no outstanding ask arrives; N asks again on the served session; the running N asks the running P.
then: The ask travels as one request toward P and nothing on stream 0, and is held by nonce; the reply settles it and the attestation becomes N's staple; the stray reply concludes nothing; on the served session nothing is sent and the ask is refused, since a light client answers no request stream; the running N's staple for X appears from P's answer on the request stream with no ask left open, and P cannot ask N. An implementation that writes a request as a stream-0 control frame fails.
interpretation: A request goes only up a session the node holds as the client; a party attached below cannot be asked, the light-client requirements asking no client to answer a request stream [author, 2026-09-11].

title: Check the structures nested in a signed body, and refuse at the public verifier what the record parser refuses

rule.text: The packed byte string MUST be exactly ceil(nibble_count / 2) bytes.
A witness's nominated_by MUST be one of the two participants.
A verifier confirms encoding, signatures, and the structural rules stated here.
a 16-byte address here is malformed in v1

given: A genuinely signed adoption whose locator claims one nibble over no bytes; a normal presence record whose witness names itself as nominator, and the same nominated by a participant; a peering whose network point carries a five-byte address; and a genuinely signed adoption without its evidence, offered to the public envelope verifier.
when: Each is parsed as a record or checked as a body; the last is verified.
then: The malformed locator, the self-nominated witness and the wide address are rejected, and the nominated record parses. The public verifier refuses the bare adoption on the body rule before any signature, with the same reason the record parser gives. An implementation that checks a locator's path only when it stands alone, or whose crypto entry point verifies signatures over a body it never checked, fails.

title: Hold a signature's declared algorithm to the profile's before verifying it

rule.text: alg lives in the protected header of whatever structure holds the signature.
Classical only

given: An endpoint record whose signature slot carries the node's genuine Ed25519 signature over a protected header declaring ML-DSA-65; a verifier response whose consent signature does the same.
when: Each is verified.
then: Both are refused: the signature is authentic, and the algorithm it declares is not the one the classical profile requires. An implementation that reads the header only for its shape and verifies with the algorithm it assumed fails.

title: Name a missing embedded signer's key as the third outcome, so the object is held and fetched for rather than discarded

rule.text: A verifier lacking one signer's key material has neither verified nor rejected the object.
Name the identity whose key is missing.
hold it, fetch the key, and let it enter

given: A genuinely signed transfer whose former patron's key the verifier lacks; a genuinely signed recovery whose verifier's key, and then whose prior key, the verifier lacks; the transfer with one byte of the former patron's block flipped under every key held; and a node receiving the transfer while holding every key but the former patron's.
when: Each is signature-checked; the node takes the object, and the key arrives.
then: Each missing key is reported as unverifiable, naming that identity, and the same objects verify once the key is held; the flipped block is invalid. The node holds the transfer pending the former patron's key, forwards nothing, and stores and forwards it when the key arrives. An implementation that reports an embedded signer's missing key as an invalid signature fails.

title: Treat a self-signed record with no signature slot, or one failing under a held key, as malformed, never as gossip

rule.text: Self-signed, and the signature's value is the same one §7.2 states
Equal seqno with different signed contents is malformed

given: An endpoint record without its signature slot; the same record with one signature byte flipped, offered to a holder that has the node's key and to one that has not; an anchor entry without its slot and one with a flipped signature under a verifying table.
when: Each is offered.
then: The slotless record is malformed whoever holds the key, and the failing signature is malformed under a held key, so neither is stored or forwarded; the failing record is stored as gossip only where the key is absent. The slotless anchor entry does not parse and the failing one is refused by the verifying table. An implementation that turns any verification error into an unavailable key fails.

title: Derive a routing slot from the settled binding, so a departure held before its adoption leaves the row empty

rule.text: Remove a child on departure or disavowal.
A minified record of every membership change travels rootward to its subnet's root.

given: P's node; N's adoption under P and N's departure from P.
when: P's node takes the departure and then the adoption; and, on another node, the adoption and then the departure.
then: In both orders the binding is closed and no row names N: taken after the held departure, the adoption's row is written empty as of the departure. An implementation that writes the child into the slot on every adoption it applies, whatever the table settled, fails.

title: Count dereferenced evidence only once its own signatures verify

rule.text: Structural verification does not dereference proof_of_presence.
That is an evaluation step, not a structural one
proof-of-presence record between these two parties

given: A valid adoption whose presence record is fetched with one signature byte flipped, its body and txid untouched; another whose witnessed presence record has a witness key the holder lacks.
when: The table applies each under required evaluation and under deferred evaluation.
then: The forged record is refused under both: a failing record is never evidence. The unverifiable record is refused under required evaluation, naming the missing key, and leaves the binding's evidence unevaluated under deferred evaluation; with every key held it satisfies. An implementation that marks fetched evidence satisfied on its type, txid and parties alone fails.

title: Keep a retired endpoint record retired across a save and a load

rule.text: a holder retains neither as current and forwards nothing further for that (subject, seqno)
Keep the topology store across a restart

given: N holding a subordinate's endpoint record at one number, saved; then the same number with different signed contents, which N takes as a conflict and saves again.
when: The store is loaded from disk.
then: The conflict marker persists, the store serves no endpoint record for that subject, and its replay carries neither record. An implementation whose save leaves the retired record's file in place, or whose load reads it back before the markers, fails.

title: Append a record already held without making its predecessor a head again

rule.text: The structure is properly a Merkle DAG, git-shaped
Branches can be merged, and merging strengthens completeness.

given: An archive holding a formation, an adoption and the departure that follows it.
when: Each of the three is appended again.
then: The archive is unchanged: one head, the departure, no fork, three records, and the next back-pointer list naming the head alone. An implementation that re-inserts a held predecessor into the head set beside its successor, reporting a fork the DAG does not have, fails.

title: Finish a frame half received when a timer or an outbound frame interrupts the read, never lose it

rule.text: Same framing as stream 0 (§8.0), same rule
Stream 0 carries length-delimited, type-tagged frames.

given: A raw peer attached to N that sends one whole heartbeat, then only the four-byte length prefix of a second; N then has an outbound frame to send on that session; the peer sends the rest of the second heartbeat.
when: N's control loop runs through the outbound send between the two fragments.
then: The outbound frame goes, and the second heartbeat is received whole afterwards: two heartbeats received, nothing discarded, the session alive. An implementation whose frame read is abandoned when another event wins, dropping the bytes it had consumed, fails.

title: Reserve capacity and store as one step, so concurrent submissions cannot exceed the recipient's cap

rule.text: At the cap, refuse the newest message and tell the sender
bounded by a per-subordinate storage cap

given: N with a one-byte cap for C and a store slow to answer how full it is; two one-byte submissions for C at once.
when: Both run.
then: Exactly one is accepted and one refused at the cap, and the store holds one message. An implementation that reads the cap and stores in two steps, so both submissions see the room for one, fails.

title: Pin only key material of the profile's shape: two keys in order, each with exactly its three labels

rule.text: of exactly two entries in fixed order
a single COSE_Key cannot represent one
the classical member of the KeyMaterial it has pinned

given: An identity's own key material; the classical key alone; the two keys in the other order; three keys; and a classical key carrying a kid label. Each variant offered with its own hash.
when: Each is pinned.
then: The identity's own material pins and yields its classical key. Every variant is refused and yields nothing: it is not an identity, whatever it hashes to. An implementation that pins anything hashing to the keyhash it was given fails.

title: Learn the server-reflexive address from the serving node acting as STUN, on the socket the direct path will use

rule.text: Infra nodes act as STUN and TURN.
Act as STUN and TURN for clients attempting direct payload paths

given: Leaf L attached to serving node S, behind an emulated NAT with endpoint-independent mapping, preparing a direct path to an in-horizon peer.
when: L gathers candidates.
then: L sends a STUN Binding Request to S at the address it serves QUIC on, S answers with the source address it saw, and L's candidates carry its host address and the reflexive address the NAT mapped for that socket.

title: Attempt the direct path first and fall back to the serving node when the checks fail

rule.text: ICE attempts the direct path first and falls back to the serving node when it fails.
ICE falls back to relaying through the serving node when hole punching fails

given: Leaves L1 and L2 inside each other's horizon, each behind an emulated NAT, having exchanged candidates through their serving nodes. The NATs' mapping and filtering behaviour is the harness's parameter.
when: L1 sends payload to L2, first with endpoint-independent NATs and then with address-and-port-dependent ones.
then: With endpoint-independent NATs a connection completes on a candidate pair and the payload crosses it with neither serving node carrying the bytes; with address-and-port-dependent NATs the checks fail within the bound and the same payload is delivered through L2's serving node.

title: Keep the relayed path a first-class route, taken whenever the direct path is not

rule.text: The relay path is not vestigial and must be maintained as a first-class route.
carry the relayed path as a first-class route rather than a fallback afterthought

given: Leaves L1 and L2 whose direct path the harness defeats, both online.
when: L1 sends L2 several messages over time while the direct path stays defeated.
then: Every message is delivered through L2's serving node in order, the relay is not retried into a failure per message, and the direct path is re-attempted only when L1 next opens a path, not on every send.
interpretation: How often a client re-attempts the direct path after a failure is not stated; the test fixes one attempt per path opening and asserts that sends in between go by the relay without delay.

title: Dial the serving node outward and never traverse for control traffic

rule.text: NAT traversal for the payload path only. Control traffic needs none: clients dial outward to their serving infra node at a static IP, and infra nodes dial each other directly.
Control traffic needs none.

given: Leaf L behind an emulated NAT, and serving node S.
when: L attaches to S, heartbeats, resolves and fetches through the session.
then: No STUN Binding Request leaves L's socket and S answers none; the session runs entirely on L's outward dial.

title: Gather no candidates and open no direct path for a peer outside the horizon

rule.text: Payload attempts a direct path inside the horizon, which does require traversal.
Direct connection is limited to the horizon

given: Leaf L1 with a peer L2 outside its horizon, both behind NATs the harness would let a direct path through.
when: L1 sends L2 payload.
then: L1 sends no STUN request, exchanges no candidates and dials no address of L2's; the payload goes by the relay.

title: Exchange addresses with the peer alone, and put no reflexive address in topology state

rule.text: The peers exchange addresses during setup and connect
a direct connection reveals each peer's IP (P17)

given: Leaves L1 and L2 inside each other's horizon, each behind a NAT, with their serving nodes recording every topology object and endpoint record they hold and forward.
when: L1 and L2 exchange candidates and connect.
then: The reflexive addresses travel only in the candidate exchange between the two leaves; no TopologyPush, EndpointRecord, memo or replicated state at either serving node carries either address.

title: Answer a query at the node hosting the verifier, for a node that is a participant and for a light client beside it

rule.text: The serving node uses it to identify which of its attached clients is meant.
The verifier checks the consent against the query's own `query_id` before anything else
a verifier answering a query about subject S sends a copy of its signed response to S as well as to the querier

given: Node N hosts two verifiers in its own process: itself, a participant answering for its own key, and light client V beside it. Querier C is attached to N over a session; subject S is beside N too and has consented within an open window.
when: C sends type-4 requests on N's request stream: one addressed to N, one to V, one to a verifier N hosts nothing for, and one naming a querier other than C. For V's, S's grant arrives on the payload channel while the stream waits.
then: N's and V's streams each carry a signed VerifierResponse from the verifier named, V's within the grant buffer rather than at its end, and S receives a copy of each over the payload channel. The other two streams fail with nothing signed.
interpretation: The documents route a query to its verifier's serving node and stop there; how that node carries it to a client attached over the wire is unwritten. The reference answers for the verifiers hosted in the node's own process, a node that is a participant for its own key and a light client beside it, and the subject's copy travels as a payload kind of the reference's own.

title: Offer candidates as their own payload kind over the relay, dial the peer's, and take the direct path from the client's own send

rule.text: The peers exchange addresses during setup and connect
ICE attempts the direct path first and falls back to the serving node when it fails.
Payload attempts a direct path inside the horizon, which does require traversal

given: Two clients inside each other's horizon, each with a payload session to the other: light clients L1 and L2 beside their serving node on sockets of their own, and nodes N1 and N2 that are participants on the nodes' own sockets. A peer outside the horizon exists.
when: L1 (and N1) offers the direct path to its peer from its own client, then sends application payload; then offers the peer outside the horizon.
then: The candidates travel through the serving node as their own payload kind; the peer dials them and offers its own back; both clients' own interfaces report the peer reachable; the application payload crosses the connection with the serving node relaying nothing further; the offer outside the horizon gathers and sends nothing.
interpretation: The candidates travel as a payload kind of the reference's own (kind 3) on whatever path exists. A light client keeps no table, so whether the path may be direct is what the node beside it says of its horizon.

title: Open an initial session only under the identity key bound to the sender it names

rule.text: Identity keys sign; encryption requires KEM keys, which are distinct and must be bound to the identity.
this profile instantiates it with X25519 and ML-KEM-768, matching the transport

given: Recipient B holds A's verified prekey bundle. C composes an initial message with C's own identity and ephemeral keys against B's bundle.
when: The message is delivered to B named as coming from A, and then the same message named as coming from C.
then: Named as A's it is refused, no session is opened for A, no plaintext is dispatched, and the person is told it could not be attributed. Named as C's it decrypts.
interpretation: The binding of a keyhash to a payload identity key is the prekey bundle, which its subject signs. A recipient holding no bundle for the sender cannot check the binding, so it refuses and asks for the bundle; that message is not recovered.

title: Spend a one-time prekey only when the message it opened authenticates

rule.text: There is directly applicable prior art, specified and formally verified. The requirement below is to adopt it, not to design a replacement.
one party offline having published prekeys, the other wanting to send immediately and establish a session

given: A sends B an initial message consuming one of B's one-time prekeys. A corrupted copy of that message, one ciphertext byte flipped, reaches B first.
when: B takes the corrupted copy, and then the original.
then: The corrupted copy fails and the one-time pair it named is still held; the original then opens the session and decrypts, and only then is the pair gone. A second message naming the same pair finds nothing.
interpretation: PQXDH's receiving procedure deletes the one-time private key after the initial message decrypts. Deleting it on arrival lets one injected copy destroy the key the real message needs.

title: Refuse a header value carrying a control character, so no caller writes a header line of its own

rule.text: Reject rather than normalise anything ambiguous
Forward what your parser produced, never the bytes you received. A byte a resource sees that your parser did not examine is a byte outside your security model.
An authenticating intermediary MUST remove every caller-controlled value in the namespace it uses for trusted identity or authorisation assertions, before inserting its own.

given: A resource request whose HTTP message carries a header whose value contains a bare LF followed by `rhtn-roles: admin`, and a second whose value carries a bare CR.
when: The gateway parses each.
then: Both are refused as ambiguous and nothing is forwarded. No serialised message reaching a backend contains an `rhtn-` header the caller wrote, whatever line ending that backend recognises.
interpretation: This parser ends a line at CRLF and a backend may end one at LF, which is the multi-parser hazard §11.2 names. The value is refused rather than stripped, since §11.2 rejects the ambiguous instead of normalising it.

title: Refuse a chunk length larger than the message rather than computing an offset past it

rule.text: Reject rather than normalise anything ambiguous: conflicting or duplicated length and transfer-encoding headers, malformed chunking

given: A chunked body whose first chunk-size line is the largest value a size can hold.
when: The gateway decodes it.
then: It returns a refusal. No offset is computed past the end of the message, in any build profile.

title: Refuse a direct path in both directions where the local decision refuses it, whoever dialled

rule.text: The peers exchange addresses during setup and connect
a direct connection reveals each peer's IP (P17)

given: Two mutually pinned peers on loopback whose local decision refuses a direct path to each other, and candidates arriving from the peer.
when: One receives the peer's candidates, and the peer dials it directly.
then: Nothing is gathered, nothing is dialled, and a connection the peer opens is closed unheld. Neither side reports the other reachable and no payload crosses a direct path.
interpretation: The decision is local and asked again at the dial and at the accept: candidates arrive from the peer, and a peer's willingness to connect is not this side's permission.

title: Reject a query from the wrong requester without disturbing a legitimate request already waiting

rule.text: Field 2 MUST name the authenticated requester
on a type-4 stream the querier is the transport-authenticated peer, and a mismatch is rejected

given: A verifier hosted in a node's process with a query pending its grant, and a second peer presenting the same signed query body under its own authenticated identity.
when: The second request is rejected.
then: The pending request keeps its place, and the grant arriving for it still completes its stream within the buffer. The rejected request gets nothing.
interpretation: The requester is checked before the request touches state another request owns, and each registration is released only by the request that made it.

title: Grant nothing outside the owner's Dunbar Org, a directional scope included

rule.text: No scope reaches outside the owner's trust horizon, `list` included
A scope naming a position outside it is not an error; it simply matches nobody the evaluator can see.

given: A chain of four nodes, the owner at one end and the asker three edges away, with the asker inside the serving node's own horizon so that guard does not stand in.
when: The owner's entry declares `Down(3)`, and the reverse chain declares `Up(3)`.
then: Neither admits the asker, and neither entry is rejected: both are stored and forwarded and grant nothing. A scope naming a party two edges away still admits it.

title: Refuse a reserved role name at the configuration boundary, so none reaches a credential

rule.text: `discover` and `connect` are reserved for the node's own evaluation (design §11.4) and never appear here
The roles you receive are application actions.

given: A package manifest declaring `connect`, `discover` and `read`, and a member's row naming the same three.
when: The manifest is instantiated and the row is set.
then: Both are refused naming the reserved name. A manifest and row of `read` alone are accepted, and the credential a backend receives carries `read` and neither reserved name.
interpretation: Refused where the operator writes it rather than filtered where it is emitted: silently dropping a role would let an operator believe they granted something.

title: Keep a routing slot a later adoption filled when a delayed ending of an earlier one arrives

rule.text: Remove a child on departure or disavowal. A stale entry refers requesters to a node that will not answer for that path.
counter incremented within the current series

given: A node holding adoption A1 of a child, then adoption A2 of the same child in a new relationship series, and then the delayed departure D1 that ends A1, dated before A2.
when: D1 is applied.
then: The table stays bound through A2 and the child's slot stays occupied, so resolution and the memo still name it. A departure ending the binding that is actually open does empty the slot, dated by that ending.
interpretation: Which relationship an ending closes is the table's answer, not the record's: the slot follows the settled bindings, as the adoption branch already did.

title: Reject a transfer whose former patron is the adopted node or the new patron

rule.text: `former_patron_key` MUST differ from adoption field 2 — identical keys represent no transfer, the same rule and the same reason as `prior_key` MUST differ from field 1 in a `Recovery` — and MUST differ from field 1
A verifier MUST check all three against the enclosing adoption

given: An adoption carrying a transfer whose former patron is the adopted node, and another whose former patron is the new patron, each with a signature that verifies under the key named.
when: Each is parsed.
then: Both are malformed at typed validation, before any signature is weighed. An adoption whose three keys are distinct still parses and verifies.
interpretation: Checkable from the adoption alone, so it sits beside the recovery block's prior-key rule rather than in a verifier that needs keys.

title: Reject a presented series chain whose reissue is timed before the record it follows

rule.text:
the current record's own floor MUST be greater than or equal
to the **effective time** of every record its key 0 list names
A node proves its current series by presenting

given: A presentation of an adoption dated 100 followed by a countersigned reissue dated 99, whose back-pointers name that adoption, with every signature verifying and the predecessor present in the chain.
when: The chain is read.
then: It is refused on chronology, as the archive's own append would refuse it. The same chain with the reissue dated 101 is accepted, and only then may it prove a series and abandon the old one.
interpretation: The predecessor is in the presentation, so this is not the unavailable-history case; the presented path is held to the rule the append path already applies.

title: Attach a late response only under consent from the ceremony of the record it supplements

rule.text: The response must carry a `query_id` the subject countersigned for that ceremony
Otherwise anyone could attach unsolicited assertions to a record naming someone else.

given: A holder keeping a record from ceremony 6 and consent given in ceremonies 6 and 7, and a correctly signed late response answering a query consented in ceremony 7.
when: The response is offered for the ceremony 6 record, and then one consented in ceremony 6 is.
then: The first is refused naming the ceremony and nothing is attached; the second is kept beside the record. A holder that keeps the record but cannot resolve its ceremony refuses too, and records the arrival with its verifier where the response verified.
interpretation: The arrival is recorded because a late response is a sign of the responder's reliability whatever became of it [author, 2026-09-12]; the bytes are not kept, since retention follows the record. A response that does not verify is not recorded, a forgery being no signal.

title: Answer a malformed resource body with status 3 rather than failing the stream

rule.text: The body decodes at all → code 3 if it does not. Nothing has been addressed yet, so answering directly discloses nothing about any resource. A malformed outer frame is a stream failure, not a response

given: An attached session sending request type 6 whose outer frame is well formed and correctly typed but whose body is an empty CBOR map, and a second stream whose outer frame itself is malformed.
when: Each is sent.
then: The first is answered `ResourceResponse` with status 3 and nothing about any resource is disclosed; the second fails its stream with no response. A malformed body on any other request type still fails its stream.
interpretation: Only the resource family has an answer defined for a body that does not decode, so the fallback is scoped to it: every other type's malformed body has no specified response and §9.2's stream failure stands.

title: Start from the operator's configuration alone, and never mint the identity it was told to read

rule.text: **Act as STUN and TURN**
**Push the sibling list at attach.**

given: A configuration naming an identity file, a peers file, a queue, a prekey directory and a topology directory, and an address to serve on.
when: The daemon is started, then started again with the identity file absent, and again with it readable beyond its owner.
then: The first serves a real session at the address it reports. The other two refuse, naming what they could not read, and exit non-zero. No identity is generated in any case.
interpretation: A node that mints a key when its file is missing serves under an identity nobody has adopted, and its operator is not told. The identity file holds the two seeds an identity is derived from; no document fixes that format, so it is the reference's.

title: Load consumable state before the first session and write it back on the way out

rule.text: **Delete on delivery, immediately, leaving nothing recoverable.**
**Keep the topology store across a restart — it is your seen-set.**

given: A daemon stopped with a signal, with material accepted for a client waiting in its queue.
when: It is restarted and that client attaches, and then it is stopped, restarted and the client attaches again.
then: The material is delivered once, on the first attach. The store then holds nothing for that client and the second attach delivers nothing.
interpretation: A node serving before it has loaded its one-time pools reissues a key it already served, and one serving before it has loaded its topology store replays a forwarding wave, so both are read before the transport accepts a session.

title: Keep a routing slot a later adoption filled when the earlier adoption it replaced arrives last

rule.text: Remove a child on departure or disavowal. A stale entry refers requesters to a node that will not answer for that path.
counter incremented within the current series

given: A node receiving, in this order, the departure that ends adoption A1 of a child, then adoption A2 of the same child in a new relationship series, and then A1 itself.
when: A1 is applied last, its own binding already ended by the departure.
then: The table stays bound through A2 and the child's slot stays occupied. Every arrival order of the same three records leaves the same table and the same slot.
interpretation: Which relationship a record changes is the table's answer and not the record's, so a row is emptied only where no open binding holds it, whichever record arrives last.

title: Refuse a direct path at an infrastructure node in both directions where the local decision refuses it

rule.text: The peers exchange addresses during setup and connect
a direct connection reveals each peer's IP (P17)

given: Two mutually pinned nodes with no topology relationship, so each lies outside the other's horizon, and the candidates of one supplied to the other by hand.
when: One is asked to gather for the other, then to open on those candidates, and then the other dials it directly.
then: Nothing is gathered, nothing is dialled, and the connection the peer opens is closed before anything on it is read. Neither node reports the other reachable.
interpretation: The gather already asked; the dial and the accept ask the same question, because candidates arrive from the peer and a peer's willingness to connect is not this node's permission.

title: Rebuild the routing view from the records a restart finds, and verify your own signature without being told your own key

rule.text: **Keep the topology store across a restart — it is your seen-set.**
Remove a child on departure or disavowal. A stale entry refers requesters to a node that will not answer for that path.

given: A daemon that accepted an adoption of a child it countersigned, holds the child in a routing slot, and has persisted. Its peers file names the other signers and not the daemon itself.
when: It is stopped and started again from those bytes.
then: The adoption verifies without the peers file naming this node, the table holds the binding, and the child occupies the slot it did before. Resubmitting the record is a duplicate and changes nothing.
interpretation: The store is the seen-set and not the view: the table, the slots and this node's own position are derived from the records it holds. A node that has been adopted takes the position its patron countersigned rather than assuming it is a root.

title: Spend a one-time key on disk before its reply goes out, so no stop can bring it back

rule.text: **Consume one-time keys on serving them**
**Only the one-time key is consumed on serving.** The reusable material may be returned any number of times to anyone.

given: A node whose pool holds one one-time key, kept in a directory, with no snapshot taken after the key is served.
when: The key is served and the node's memory is then lost, and a node is started again from the bytes on disk.
then: The pool is empty and the key is not served a second time. A key whose file cannot be removed is not served at all, and the reusable material alone is answered.
interpretation: A snapshot taken after the reply cannot carry once-only issuance: a stop between snapshots would return a key whose private half the recipient has already consumed. The allowance counters are spent with the key for the same reason, a counter kept only in memory giving a requester a fresh window every time the process stops.

title: Decode every object the corpus carries with the parser a node uses, and say which are unverifiable rather than failing

rule.text: **A back-pointer whose record is unavailable is not a failure.**

given: Every byte-class entry in `test-vectors/corpus.json`, and a tool holding no identities.
when: Each is decoded under the kind the corpus declares for it.
then: Each prints its shape and its verdict. What the corpus expects accepted is never reported refused; what it expects refused is never reported clean; and a signed object no key is held for is reported unverifiable rather than failing.
interpretation: The tool decodes with the parser a node uses and no other: a second, laxer decoder written for convenience would disagree with the first invisibly.

title: Ask a running node only the questions that change nothing

rule.text: **Read-only lookups are unaffected** — resolution, archive fetch and catalog queries answer the same way however often they are replayed

given: A running node with a subordinate, its own archive and an empty catalog, and a tool attached to it as a member of its horizon.
when: The tool resolves the subordinate, fetches the node's archive and queries its catalog, and then is asked to send something else.
then: Each of the three is answered and printed, the archive naming the records it holds. Anything outside the read-only class is refused by the tool before it dials.
interpretation: A prekey fetch consumes a one-time key and a resource request has an application effect whatever the method inside, so neither is reachable from a command whose purpose is to look.

title: A snapshot holds what is held: a served one-time key does not survive the save that follows it

rule.text: **Consume one-time keys on serving them**
**Only the one-time key is consumed on serving.** The reusable material may be returned any number of times to anyone.

given: A prekey service loaded from a directory it is not bound to, holding one one-time key.
when: The key is served, the service is saved, and a service is loaded from that directory again.
then: The pool is empty and no key is served a second time. The reusable material is still there, and a subject whose bundle the service no longer holds is gone from the directory too. The allowance a requester has spent is still spent after a restart.
interpretation: One rule whichever way the service is kept: the save makes the directory match what is held. A bound service already has disk and memory in step and loses nothing to it; a detached one is snapshotted, and adding without removing would leave a served key for the next load to hand out.

title: A reissue advances the relationship it names, so a departure in the proven current series ends it

rule.text: counter incremented within the current series
**The new series MUST NOT be one the node has previously occupied.**

given: A table holding an adoption in series 1, then the patron-countersigned reissue leaving series 1 for series 2, then a departure naming series 2.
when: Each is applied in that order, and separately with the reissue arriving before its adoption.
then: The reissue leaves the relationship open and moves it into series 2; the departure then ends it, and the node is no longer a subordinate. A reissue arriving first is held and settles when its adoption does. A departure naming series 1 after the reissue ends nothing, and a re-adoption opening its own series is a different binding the reissue never touched.
interpretation: The series left is what identifies the relationship a reissue advances, not the larger number: succession is proved by the countersigned chain, and a re-adoption that happens to open a higher series is a binding of its own.

title: A restart puts back this node's own chain from the archive it keeps, and the series its relationship is now in

rule.text: **Keep the topology store across a restart — it is your seen-set.**
A signer with no prior transaction uses the genesis value

given: A node that has signed and stored a record of its own, and whose relationship a stored patron-countersigned reissue has moved into a later series.
when: It is stopped and started again from those bytes.
then: Its next back-pointer names the record it signed rather than genesis, so the next record it signs extends the chain it published. Its own locator carries the series the reissue entered, not the one it left.
interpretation: A key's own archive is not its topology store and is not derived from one [author, 2026-09-13]: the store is a seen-set the horizon bounds, and the archive is the key's own signed history from its first transaction, which nothing prunes. They are persisted apart.

title: Verify an archive batch's own links before reporting it, and say that newestness is not among them

rule.text: **The requester verifies the chain itself.** Each returned record's back-pointers must match the record that follows it in the batch
**A holder cannot be trusted to have walked correctly**

given: A node answering an archive fetch, serving first a connected two-record batch and then two individually valid records that both point at genesis.
when: The requester takes each reply.
then: The connected batch is reported with its records, and says that newestness is the holder's claim because no head was requested. The disconnected batch is refused, naming the record whose back-pointers do not reach the one that follows it.
interpretation: The subject's own back-pointer list is the one that must match: a record carries one per signer, and only the subject's continues the subject's chain. Newestness stays uncheckable where no head was named, and saying so is part of not overclaiming.

title: A shell drives the client through the boundary, and every answer including a refusal is a value

rule.text: **Obtain the strongest proximity channel the hardware supports**
**Run the guided capture sequence.**

given: A shell supplying the proximity hardware, camera, clock, randomness, operator and notice sink as objects, and a client started behind them on a thread of its own.
when: The shell opens a ceremony, takes the counterparty's intent, runs the channels, and then passes an identity of the wrong length and a platform whose randomness gives short measure.
then: The client is the identity it was given, the intent crosses as fields, the channels come back strongest first with the one that failed reported failed and nothing promoted, and each bad input comes back as a refusal carrying its reason rather than as a process that vanished.
interpretation: The ceremony's own conversation between two present devices has no encoding any document fixes, so an intent crosses as fields for the shell to carry however the two devices manage. Randomness of short measure is refused rather than padded, a seed completed with zeroes not being one.

title: A publication is taken only from the subject the bundle names

rule.text: The node refuses a publication whose subject is not the authenticated requester.
Take a prekey publication only from the subject it names

given: Node N serves clients S and T. S holds a prekey bundle signed by S; T holds one signed by T.
when: T sends a type-9 PrekeyPublication on its own request stream carrying S's bundle, and then one carrying its own.
then: The first reply echoes T's nonce with code 1 and N holds no bundle for S from it; the second echoes its nonce with code 0 and N holds T's bundle.

title: A publication and a deposit from an attached client are held and served

rule.text:
It cannot publish its own
prekey bundle, stock its own one-time pool, hold its own mail, or be woken by a
service it is not connected to.
The bundle is opaque to this protocol

given: Client S is attached to node N over a session and N holds nothing for S.
when: S sends a type-9 publication of its own bundle and a type-10 deposit of k one-time keys.
then: Both replies echo their nonces with code 0, and a later type-3 fetch of S from any requester returns that bundle byte for byte and one of the deposited keys.

title: A deposit past the node's bound is refused whole, and the pool is unchanged

rule.text: a node applies its own storage bound on top: the pool is space it lends
a client that asks for more than you lend is refused with the code rather than silently trimmed

given: Node N lends a pool of p keys per client and client S is attached with q keys already stocked.
when: S deposits more than p minus q keys in one type-10 request.
then: The reply echoes S's nonce with code 2, and N's pool for S still holds exactly q keys.

title: A relay submission is answered when the node takes it, not when it is delivered

rule.text: The answer says the node took it, which is the same promise design §14.1.6's queue makes

Answer a relay submission when you have taken it, not when you have
  delivered it.

given: Node N serves clients S and R. R holds no session with N and is not reachable.
when: S submits ciphertext for R in a type-11 request.
then: The reply echoes S's nonce with code 0 before R has connected; N's queue for R holds one message; and when R attaches it receives that message with S's keyhash in front of the ciphertext unchanged.

title: A relay submission for a keyhash the node holds no record of is refused

rule.text: The node refuses one for a recipient it holds no record of
the node distinguishing "offline" from "no record"

given: Node N serves client S and holds no record of keyhash U.
when: S submits ciphertext for U in a type-11 request.
then: The reply echoes S's nonce with code 1, N queues nothing, and the answer is distinguishable at S from the code returned for a recipient N serves who is merely offline.

title: One wake endpoint per relationship, replaced on re-registration

rule.text: A node keeps at most one per relationship
The endpoint is what the patron holds, and it is all the patron needs

given: Client S is attached to node N and has registered no endpoint.
when: S sends a type-12 registration carrying endpoint E1 with its key, then a second carrying E2 with a different key.
then: Both replies echo their nonces with code 0, and N holds exactly one endpoint for S, which is E2 with E2's key.

title: A registration with no endpoint withdraws, and a key without one is malformed

rule.text: An endpoint's key and lapse describe an endpoint; carrying either without one would be a shape with no meaning, and a decoder rejects it.

A registration with no
  endpoint withdraws

given: Client S is attached to node N with endpoint E registered.
when: S sends a type-12 registration with field 2 absent, then one with field 2 absent and field 3 present.
then: The first reply echoes its nonce with code 0 and N holds no endpoint for S; the second is rejected by the decoder and never reaches the register.

title: Every reply echoes the request's nonce and says nothing else

rule.text: A client learns that its node took what it said; the node discloses nothing about the other clients it serves, and a refusal names no reason

given: Client S is attached to node N.
when: S sends one of each of the four request types, each with a distinct nonce, some of which N refuses.
then: Each reply is a two-field map whose field 1 is the nonce of the request that drew it and whose field 2 is one of 0, 1 and 2; no reply carries any other field.

title: A wake folds in what arrived since, rather than replaying the store

rule.text: the whole transaction history must not be replayed on every wake
Store the fold's result with a watermark that says which records produced it.

given: A node has run, accepted a set of topology records, and written its store and its derived view.
when: It is stopped, further records are added to its store, and it is started again.
then: The table, the routing slots and the node's own position are what a full replay of the whole store would produce, and only the records above the derived view's watermark went through the fold.

title: A derived view that cannot account for the store is discarded whole

rule.text: A materialised copy carries enough to say whether it is still current, and is discarded whole when it cannot.
Discard a derived view that cannot account for your store, and replay.

given: A node with a written store and a written derived view.
when: The derived view is damaged, or a record is added to the store that sorts at or below the view's watermark, and the node is started.
then: The view is discarded, the whole store is replayed, and the resulting table and slots equal what a node with no derived view at all would hold.

title: A client places every node in its horizon from what its patron propagated

rule.text: A participant holds enough of its horizon to resolve every node in it directly
Persist enough to resolve every node in your trust horizon directly

given: A light client attached to a serving node that floods it the adoptions forming a subtree around it.
when: The client is asked where each node it holds a record for sits, and how far away each is, with its serving node unreachable. The copy is then pruned.
then: Every node within a two-edge walk is placed from the client's own state and its distance equals the number of adoption or sibling edges to it; a node beyond the walk has no distance, and a party in no record at all has neither a place nor a distance. A prune then drops every party the horizon does not hold, and a second prune has nothing left to do.

title: A wake folds in what arrived since, and an unaccountable snapshot is discarded

rule.text: A materialised copy carries enough to say whether it is still current, and is discarded whole when it cannot.

Discard the copy whole when its watermark cannot account for what you
  hold

given: A client holding propagated records and a materialised copy of the shape they produce.
when: It wakes with that copy, then wakes with one that is damaged, one claiming more records than it holds, and none at all.
then: The first folds in only the records above the copy's watermark; each of the others replays every record held; and all four leave the same table and the same locators.

title: The propagated version is the system of record, and replaces what was held

rule.text: The propagated version is always the system of record

where the two differ,
  the propagated version wins and yours is rewritten

given: A client holding a locator for a node, learned from an earlier propagation.
when: Its serving node propagates a later record placing that node somewhere else, and then a record ending a binding the client holds.
then: The client answers with the later locator and not the earlier, the ended binding is gone from its table, and nothing the client held before is preferred to what was propagated.

title: A client learns its horizon from the flood its serving node forwards

rule.text: your serving node, and the clients attached to you

What a
participant keeps is a copy of what its patron infrastructure provided

given: A light client attached to a serving node, holding no topology.
when: The node sends topology pushes on stream 0, interleaved with a memo, a push whose body kind is not a transaction, and a frame that is not a push at all.
then: Every transaction carried in a topology push is in the client's horizon and placed; none of the other three is; and the client's reader is still running afterwards.

title: The socket that answers STUN does not flatten what the kernel coalesces

rule.text: Infra nodes act as STUN and TURN.
Act as STUN and TURN for clients attempting direct payload paths

given: A node serving QUIC on the same socket it answers STUN Binding requests on, and a peer with a session to it.
when: The peer sends messages of one, twenty-five and two hundred thousand bytes, each spanning many datagrams.
then: Every message crosses whole and once, within a bound no per-packet retransmission could meet. A socket that handed several coalesced arrivals to the receiver as one datagram would deliver the first packet of each batch and lose the rest.

title: The kernel holds the session, and no wire byte crosses to the shell

rule.text: One participant, one kernel
Publish your bundle and stock your pool as part of attaching

given: A shell holding only the facade, and a serving node on the network.
when: The shell attaches, registers and withdraws a wake endpoint, sends payload to another client of that node, and asks for what arrived.
then: The node holds the bundle and pool the attach published, the endpoint the registration gave and then nothing after the withdrawal, and the recipient's shell is handed the payload already decrypted. No method returns an encoding, and maintenance without a session is refused with its reason.

title: A structured field is the object the grammar names, never a byte string wrapping it

rule.text: 1: PrekeyBundle,             ; §7.8's bundle, signed by its subject
The bundle is opaque to this protocol

given: A decoder holding the grammar for a request type whose field is declared as a structured object.
when: It is given that field encoded as a byte string wrapping the object's own encoding, and then encoded as the object itself.
then: The wrapping is refused and the object accepted. A decoder that wraps on the way out and unwraps on the way in round-trips against itself and fails against every conformant peer, which no self-test can see.

title: A value outside a declared range is refused, never narrowed to fit

rule.text: series    = uint                   ; U32 RANGE. ARBITRARY, never ordered
Unknown *values* in a known enumerated field MUST be rejected

given: A decoder reading a locator whose series and counter the grammar bounds to the u32 range.
when: It is given a series of 2^32 and a counter of 2^32.
then: Both are refused as malformed. Narrowing either to fit would leave two parties holding different beliefs about which series a node is on, with nothing raised on either side, which is worse than a rejection.

title: A conditional field stands or falls with the field it describes

rule.text: An endpoint's key and lapse describe an endpoint; carrying either without one would be a shape with no meaning, and a decoder rejects it.

given: A decoder reading a wake registration.
when: It is given a registration with no endpoint but a key, one with no endpoint but a lapse, one with an endpoint and no key, and a withdrawal carrying the nonce alone.
then: The first three are refused and the withdrawal accepted, at the decoder rather than at a node's policy.

title: Serving a one-time key leaves no record of who asked for whose bundle

rule.text:
serve the request,
  keep no record of who asked for whose bundle.
an ordinary fetch names a population rather than a person and carries no intent signal

given: A node whose prekey service is kept on disk, holding a published bundle and a stocked pool for a subject.
when: A requester is served a one-time key, the node writes its state back, and the rate-limit window later expires.
