then: Nothing anywhere under the node's directories contains the requester's keyhash beside the subject's, at any point. The allowance still binds within a window in memory, and a restart opens a fresh one, which costs the rate and not the budget since a served key is unlinked before its reply.

title: A deposit the node cannot store whole is refused, not acknowledged

rule.text: A deposit is bounded by the array limits like everything else
a client that asks for more than you lend is refused with the code rather than silently trimmed

given: A node serving a client whose bundle it holds, with its prekey service kept somewhere it cannot write.
when: The client deposits one-time keys.
then: The reply refuses, the pool holds none of the deposited keys, and nothing partially written survives. A client is never told a pool was replenished that was not.

title: Serving a one-time key does not stop the node writing its state back

rule.text: Keep the topology store across a restart — it is your seen-set.
Consume one-time keys on serving them

given: A daemon started from a configuration, holding a published bundle and a stocked pool.
when: It serves a one-time key to a requester and then writes its state back, twice.
then: Both saves succeed, and the archive, the topology store and the derived view are all on disk afterwards. Ordinary issuance is not a condition that can stop a node persisting.

title: A relationship that ends takes the wake endpoint with it

rule.text:
Forget an endpoint when the relationship ends, and when a client
  withdraws it.
a cache with no expiry is a retention decision made by omission

given: A node holding a wake endpoint for a client it serves, registered over the client's own session.
when: The relationship ends: by the client's departure, by the node's disavowal of it, and by a recovery that supersedes the client's key.
then: The endpoint is gone in each case, as it is on an explicit withdrawal, and the routing slot is empty. A registration that outlived its relationship would be a routable identifier for a person held past the reason it was given.

title: A message the serving node refused reaches the application as unsent

rule.text: Refusals are values that carry their reason.
The reply carries the nonce and a code and nothing further.

given: A shell attached to a serving node that will not queue for the recipient, whose prekey material the client holds.
when: The shell sends application payload to that recipient.
then: The call reports a refusal rather than success, nothing is queued at the node, and the same discipline applies to publishing a bundle and stocking a pool. An application told a message was sent stops retrying it.

title: A fold is reused only over the record set it was taken from

rule.text: A materialised copy carries enough to say whether it is still current, and is discarded whole when it cannot.

Store
  the fold's result with a watermark that says which records produced it.

given: A party holding a materialised copy of the shape a set of records produced.
when: One of those records is replaced by a different one, and the party wakes with the copy.
then: The copy is discarded and the whole set replayed, and the resulting view is what the records held actually say. A watermark that counted records rather than naming them would be satisfied by the substitution, since the count and the last record are unchanged.

title: A replay does not resurrect a party that left the horizon

rule.text: Keep it bounded by the horizon
A horizon is every node within a two-edge walk of you

given: A client holding the records that placed a party, and a later record ending that relationship.
when: The party's place is read, the copy is pruned, and the whole record set is then replayed.
then: The party is not placed at any point after the relationship ended, and the replayed view answers exactly as the incremental one did. The records that placed it are still held, so a bound applied only at pruning time would be undone by the replay.

title: A derived view belonging to another identity is discarded

rule.text: Discard a derived view that cannot account for your store, and replay.

What a
participant keeps is a copy of what its patron infrastructure provided

given: Two nodes holding the same topology records, whose own subordinate slots therefore differ.
when: One node is started with the other's derived view beside its store.
then: The view is discarded and the node rebuilds its own table and its own routing slots. Installing another party's fold would replace this node's slots with theirs, which is a different node's answer to a question only this node can answer.

title: A running node learns who is attached to it, and forwards to them

rule.text: your serving node, and the clients attached to you
Attachment answers one question: where do my messages queue.

given: A running node with no topology relationships recorded, and a client that attaches to it.
when: A transaction in the node's store reach arrives from a third party, and the client's session later ends.
then: The node stores it and forwards it to the attached client, and treats the client's own transactions as within its store. After the session ends it forwards nothing further to that party. A node told nothing about its attaches holds an empty set and serves the flood to none of its clients, whatever its configuration says.

title: A transaction crosses two daemon processes and survives a restart

rule.text: Keep the topology store across a restart — it is your seen-set.

a node forwards a stored transaction to every adjacent node
except the one it arrived from

given: Two daemon processes started from their own configuration files, one naming the other as its patron, with nothing pre-seeded in either.
when: A transaction is pushed into the first over a session, and the second is later stopped and started again.
then: It reaches the second over the session between the two processes, is in that process's store on disk after it stops, and the restarted process still holds the binding it needs to accept a further transaction. Nothing here reads a view: every claim is made over a session or from what the process wrote.

title: A daemon answers a resolution from the topology it was pushed

rule.text: Published by infra nodes only.

reconciliation is a
replay of the same frames rather than a distinct mechanism

A node refers when the
path leads into another infra node's subtree, and answers when it does not.

given: A daemon process started with nothing pre-seeded, and a client attached to it over a session.
when: Two adoptions are pushed into it over a session, a second process is then started as the subject of the first adoption, a resolution is requested for the party at the end of the path, and a further client attaches after every record has arrived.
then: It answers on the stream with the nonce it was asked with, and refers to the second process rather than serving for itself, because that process published an endpoint record and only infra nodes publish. The referral advances at least one nibble and names where to reach the next hop. The client that attached late is replayed the records it never saw arrive. A subject on a path it holds no record for is a stated failure rather than a hang or a silence.
interpretation: A session coming up is where the replay happens. The section also asks for a periodic reconciliation with siblings and patron, whose interval no document states; that half is not implemented.

title: A package reaching past the two bindings is not admitted

rule.text: No host binding exposes network transaction primitives to a package.
A plugin receives exactly the host bindings it is granted and nothing else

given: A host offering a package two bindings, its request and its response, and no others.
when: Packages are presented that import a dataset the host holds, a platform capability, or a hook inside the host's own instance that the host does not have.
then: Each is refused before it is instantiated, and the refusal names what was asked for rather than reporting a link failure. A package importing nothing is admitted, so the refusal is about the request and not about the sandbox. A package the host cannot call, and bytes that are not a component, are refused as what they are.
interpretation: The instance the two bindings live in, and the entry the host calls, are the reference implementation's names; no document fixes them.

title: A package is handed its request and gives back its answer

rule.text:
and its own request traffic, and nothing else: no topology, no liveness state,
no queue contents, no prekey requests, no role-evaluation inputs
The resource never reads network state.

given: An admitted package that hands back what it is given.
when: Two requests are served through it in turn, and a package that answers nothing is served once.
then: It sees the message the node built and nothing beside it, and the second request is not the first one's. A package that answers nothing has answered nothing, and the host does not invent a body for it.

title: A package that will not stop is stopped, and costs the next caller nothing

rule.text: one that cannot be confined cannot be contained
not meeting a package's requirements is ordinary capacity, not a conformance failure

given: A package that never returns, and a package that breaks, each admitted with a budget for one request.
when: Each is served, and a working package on the same host is served after them.
then: The one that will not stop is stopped and reported as having spent its budget; the one that breaks is reported as a defect, which is the different fact an operator acts on differently. Each request carries its own budget, so a second attempt is stopped again rather than inheriting the first one's exhaustion, and the working package is unaffected.
interpretation: What one request may spend is an operator's number. No document fixes a figure, and the reference's defaults are a starting point rather than a rule.

title: A package that grows without bound is bounded

rule.text: one that cannot be confined cannot be contained

A node that cannot meet
those requirements cannot host you, and remains conforming

given: A package that grows its memory until it is refused, and a package that answers with more than the host will carry.
when: Each is served under a stated ceiling.
then: The growing package is refused more memory rather than trapping the host, and stops at the ceiling it was given rather than at one it chose. The oversized answer is refused as an answer, with its size stated, rather than reported as a defect in the package.

title: A stopped package is unavailable rather than broken

rule.text: You may decline to host a package you cannot support.

A node that cannot meet
those requirements cannot host you, and remains conforming

given: An admitted package serving requests.
when: The host stops it without unbinding it.
then: It reports itself as not running, which is the question the gateway asks before it hands anything over, and a request that reaches it anyway is refused rather than served.

title: What reaches a package through the gateway is the credential and the request

rule.text: The credential travels as request headers

The node evaluates access and presents
the result as a credential; the resource sees an authenticated principal holding
roles

given: A gateway with a sandboxed package bound to it, and a row granting the requester connect and one application role.
when: A resource request is evaluated and handed on.
then: What crosses is the four credential headers, the authority the node addressed the package by, and the requester's own request. Nothing about the network crosses with it.

title: A daemon hosts the package its configuration names, and serves a request to it

rule.text:
A package must
declare its roles, tolerate the sandbox, and accept the node's credential
The credential travels as request headers

given: A daemon process whose configuration names a hosting file, and a package on disk beside its manifest.
when: A client attached to that process sends a resource request for the resource the file names, and then for one it does not.
then: The process admits the package before it serves, runs it, and answers on the stream with what the package returned. What crossed into the package is the credential headers, the authority the node addressed it by and the requester's own request, and nothing about the network. A resource nothing was bound for is refused rather than answered. A hosting file naming a package the sandbox would not admit stops the process from starting, and the operator is told which binding it would not give.
interpretation: The hosting file's shape is the reference implementation's, in the same class as the configuration format section 7 leaves to the author.

title: A manifest that does not describe its component is refused

rule.text: Capability declaration in the manifest
Declare what you need in the manifest.

given: A package whose component reaches both host bindings.
when: It is presented with a manifest that declares neither, one that declares a binding the host does not have, and manifests that are missing a component, repeat a key, carry an unknown key, or claim a reserved role.
then: Each is refused before the package is bound, and the operator is shown both what the manifest declared and what the component reaches. A manifest that says what its component does is admitted.
interpretation: Agreement between a manifest and its component is not a supply chain: signing, provenance and the update channel are what §9.1 leaves open, and none of them is here.

title: A grant is checked against the package before anything is bound

rule.text:
the operator hears about it at configuration time, never a requester at request
time

discover and connect are
reserved for the node's own evaluation (design §11.4) and never appear here

given: A hosting file binding a package that declares two roles.
when: Grants are written for a role the package did not declare, for a name reserved to the node's own evaluation, and for a resource no line hosts, and a file is presented whose last line is refused.
then: Each is refused at configuration with the line and the name, rather than at request time. A file refused anywhere in it binds nothing from anywhere else in it. A grant of the declared roles is applied, and a grant without connect is a row an operator may write.

title: An endpoint record is what says its publisher is infrastructure

rule.text: Published by infra nodes only.

A node refers when the
path leads into another infra node's subtree, and answers when it does not.

given: A node holding a subtree three edges deep, whose table marks nobody but itself as infrastructure.
when: An endpoint record for a node inside its store reach arrives, and one for a node outside it, and the table is later rebuilt from the store alone.
then: Holding the record is what marks its publisher, so the nearest infrastructure node above a party below it moves from this node to the publisher. A record outside store reach marks nothing, because the mark follows storage and never the wire. A rebuild reaches the same set from the store, and does not lose the node's own mark.
interpretation: There is no unmarking: §7.6 gives a record a successor and no retraction, so a node that stopped being infrastructure leaves its records standing in every horizon that stored them.

title: Two participant processes exchange payload through a daemon

rule.text: Publish a prekey bundle and keep it stocked.

A batch request names the population it sweeps; a single-subject
request is visibly targeted

given: A node process started from its own configuration, and two participant processes each started from an identity file and told nothing else.
when: One attaches and publishes, the other attaches naming it and sweeps it, the first attaches again naming the second, and payload is sent.
then: Each attach reports the node it reached and that the session is the primary one. The payload comes out of the recipient's events decrypted, having crossed two sockets and a process that never held the plaintext. Nothing is asserted from inside a process: every claim is what one printed or what arrived at one.
interpretation: The order of the three attaches is the protocol's: a bundle must be published before it can be swept, and a recipient attributes an initial message only under a binding it already holds.

title: An instrument reports what it was told the hardware did, and nothing more

rule.text:
Obtain the strongest proximity channel the hardware supports, and record
  which was achieved. Never present a weaker channel as a stronger one

given: A participant process running on a machine with no proximity radio and no camera pointed at anybody.
when: Channels are declared, cleared, and asked about, and commands are given that name no channel and no identity.
then: It supports nothing until something is declared, reports declarations strongest first, promotes none of them, and treats a cleared channel as unsupported again. The standing answer to a question put to the person is to decline. A command it does not understand is refused with what was wrong, not ignored.
interpretation: A declaration is evidence about a scenario rather than about hardware, which is the whole difference between an instrument and a client, and is why this claims none of the product entries.

title: A ceremony runs to a record between four processes

rule.text:
Nominate witnesses only from the counterparty's neighbourhood, never from your
  own

each seals its captures of the
other party under the key that party supplied, discarding it once the capture is
sealed.

given: Four participant processes, each started from its own identity file and told nothing else, two of them meeting and two nominated to witness.
when: The ceremony is run a step at a time, each step's product carried between processes the way a screen and a camera would otherwise carry it.
then: Both devices name the ceremony the same thing, the counterparty weighs the channels the other achieved, each captures the other under the key that party supplied, each nominee answers its own nominator's ask, and the record is proposed, signed by both participants over the disclosures and by both witnesses without them, and finalised. Every signer names the same record.
interpretation: The token each step produces is this instrument's encoding, not the protocol's: design §7 has the ceremony cross whatever channel the two devices have and fixes none, which is why the boundary carries it as fields.
